issues.title: [RFC]: vLLM NaN Reporting
issues.body_head:
# RFC: KV Cache NaN Detection

## Motivation

We discovered that R1 NVFP4 had issues with NaNs in the forward pass. While debugging, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43318 was created to aid debugging, which helped us find and fix the following NaN-inducing bugs:

* https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39444: dummy run writing NaN to KV cache null block
* https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38148: FP8 scale buffers allocated with torch.empty instead of torch.zeros
* https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42984: SiLU-Mul quant kernel spreading NaN across row boundaries
* https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/40047: broader sweep of kernels spreading NaN across rows (silu_and_mul_scaled_nvfp4_experts_quantize, scaled_fp4_grouped_quantize)
* https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP/issues/621: DeepEP low-latency combine race condition producing incorrect results at batch size 512+
* https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP/pull/632: proposed fix for the above
* https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/2861: FlashInfer mm_fp4 NaN sensitivity with 8x4 SF layout
* https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3103: grouped_gemm_nt_masked spreading NaN across row boundaries
* https://github.com/tlrmchlsmth/vllm/pull/33: CUDA graph NaN padding tests for attention/MoE/per-token ops

Also related: https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/issues/1974, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/35219

The main challenge when debugging NaNs in logits is **causality**. When a NaN gets into the KV cache by any of the above mechanisms, it produces NaNs at the next generation step. By the time the NaN shows up in logits, the originating layer, phase, and step are lost. Therefore, causality is the most important design goal for this RFC.

`VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS=1` added logits NaN reporting in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/30187. We wanted to expand on this capability, so we created https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43318 which covers broad kernel-side NaN/Inf detection and was used to debug the above issues. It won't get merged since it was hacked up together and is too intrusive. However, the following Grafana dashboard was created using metrics generated by that PR:

![KV Cache NaN Debug Dashboard](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aca0e4c8-e59c-4a6b-9944-dd00be9554a2)

issues.title: [Bug]: marlin_gemm shape mismatch (size_k doubled) for google/gemma-4-12B-it-qat-w4a16-ct on vLLM v0.22.0
issues.body_head:
## Your current environment

- **vLLM version**: v0.22.0+cu129
- **GPU**: NVIDIA L40S (46 GB VRAM)
- **CUDA**: 12.8 (driver 570.124.06)
- **Python**: 3.12
- **Model**: google/gemma-4-12B-it-qat-w4a16-ct (compressed-tensors W4A16)

## 🐛 Describe the bug

When serving `google/gemma-4-12B-it-qat-w4a16-ct` with `vllm serve` on v0.22.0, the engine crashes on the first real forward pass with a Marlin GEMM shape mismatch:

```
RuntimeError: Shape mismatch: a.size(1) = 4096, size_k = 8192
  torch.ops._C.marlin_gemm.default(
      reinterpret_tensor(arg0_1, (570, 4096), ...),
      size_m=570, size_n=3840, size_k=8192, ...
  )
```

Crashes identically with and without `--enforce-eager` (no torch.compile frames in traceback).

## Root cause (updated after deeper investigation)

**vLLM v0.22.0 has no native `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration` support** — the architecture was added in PR #44429 which is not in v0.22.0 or v0.22.1. vLLM falls back to the generic `TransformersMultiModalForCausalLM` wrapper (confirmed in logs: `WARNING: TransformersMultiModalForCausalLM has no VLLM implementation, falling back to Transformers implementation`).

The generic Transformers wrapper in `vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py` unconditionally applies `quant_config` to **every** `nn.Linear` it finds, including `vision_embedder.patch_dense`. The checkpoint's compressed-tensors ignore list (`model.vision_embedder.patch_dense`) never matches because the qual_name the wrapper assigns differs from the ignore pattern.

Result: `patch_dense` gets quantized when the checkpoint contains plain unquantized weights for it → wrong packed weight shape → `size_k=8192` (doubled from the real 4096) passed to `marlin_gemm`.

This is the same underlying issue as PR #44571 (`[Bugfix] Exclude vision embedder from quantization in Gemma4 Unified`), but PR #44571 patches the **native** `gemma4_unified.py` introduced in PR #44429 — code that doesn't exist in v0.22.0. The Transformers fallback path in v0.22.0 hits the same bug through a different code location.

## Fix

The fix is in `main` via:
- **PR #44429**: adds native `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration` support, bypassing the Transformers fallback entirely
- **PR #44571**: fixes the `patch_dense` prefix/quant propagation in the native implementation

Neither is included in v0.22.0 or v0.22.1 (v0.22.1 release notes confirm it only contains unrelated fixes).

## Workaround for v0.22.0 users

Hotpatch the native implementation from `ma

issues.title: [Bug]: ROCm MI300X FP8 KV cache MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 accuracy issues
issues.body_head:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Key environment details</summary>

```text
GPU              : 8x AMD Instinct MI300X (gfx942)
Image            : vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:minimax-m3
vLLM             : 0.22.1rc1.dev490+g4a560dd8d
Model            : MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8
Model dtype      : torch.bfloat16
Quantization     : mxfp8
Attention backend: TRITON_ATTN
Parallelism      : TP=8, expert parallelism enabled
KV cache         : fp8 (broken) / auto-BF16 (working)
Prefix caching   : disabled
```

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

### Summary

On ROCm/MI300X, `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` starts successfully with
`--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, and requests return HTTP 200, but generated output is
severely corrupted.

vLLM also reports that calibrated FP8 attention scales are unavailable and
uses `1.0`:

```text
Using uncalibrated q_scale 1.0 and/or prob_scale 1.0 with fp8 attention.
This may cause accuracy issues. Please make sure q/prob scaling factors are
available in the fp8 checkpoint.
```

That warning was initially suspected, but it is not the cause of this failure.
The failure is a dtype mismatch in the MiniMax-M3 sparse-attention path.

This is not a small accuracy regression. GSM8K strict accuracy drops from
`0.9666` with the default BF16 KV cache to `0.0099` with FP8 KV cache.
Outputs contain unrelated problem fragments, incorrect arithmetic, and
repetition that often continues to the generation limit.

Removing only `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` restores normal output and accuracy.

This appears related to #45533, but the failure mode is different: #45533
reports startup failure, while this configuration starts and serves normally
but silently returns incorrect output.

### Root cause

On ROCm gfx942, `current_platform.fp8_dtype()` is
`torch.float8_e4m3fnuz`. The MiniMax-M3 sparse backend instead hardcodes
`torch.float8_e4m3fn` when it reinterprets the byte-backed KV cache:

```python
self.kv_cache_fp8_dtype = (
    torch.float8_e5m2
    if "e5m2" in kv_cache_dtype
    else torch.float8_e4m3fn
)
```

The prefill and decode wrappers also classify only `float8_e4m3fn` and
`float8_e5m2` as FP8, omitting `float8_e4m3fnuz`.

FN and FNUZ do not have the same encoding. Interpreting gfx942 FNUZ KV-cache
bytes as FN changes the represented values before sparse attention consumes
them. A direct MI300X kernel comparison measured:

| KV interpretation | Relative L2 error | Cosine similarity | Output norm ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Correct FNUZ | 0.0387

issues.title: [Bug][KV Offload]: `on_request_finished()` has inconsistent guarantees across offloading layers
issues.body_head:
### Your current environment

N/A — this is a semantic/contract bug in internal APIs, not a runtime failure.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Follow-up to #45823 (*[KV offload] Defer on_request_finished until in-flight transfers drain*).

**The bug:** `on_request_finished` has inconsistent guarantees across the two offloading layers:

- `OffloadingManager.on_request_finished` fires after GPU→CPU stores have **completed** (and the CPU→secondary cascades have been submitted).
- `SecondaryTierManager.on_request_finished` fires after the CPU→secondary `submit_store`s have only been **submitted**, not completed.

One hook carries a "completion" guarantee and the other a "submission" guarantee.

**Expected behavior:** a uniform contract per layer:

> `on_request_finished` at layer *X* = "*X* will receive no more **submit** calls for this request." 
> Completion callbacks and in-flight transfers may still occur afterward.

Each layer should fire when *its own* submissions are done:

- `OffloadingManager` → after the request's last `prepare_store`/`prepare_load` (its GPU↔CPU "submit" calls), ≈ at request stop.
- `SecondaryTierManager` → after the request's last `submit_store`/`submit_load`, i.e. after the last `complete_store` that triggers the cascade.

**Suggested fix:**

1. **Connector** (`OffloadingConnectorScheduler`): fire `OffloadingManager.on_request_finished` eagerly in `request_finished()` (revert the completion-deferral), once the request's last `prepare_store` has been issued. Care needed: under async scheduling a final block's store can be deferred, so the connector must ensure it is submitted before firing.
2. **`TieringOffloadingManager`**: stop delegating to `tier.on_request_finished` immediately. Track per-request outstanding GPU→CPU stores (`prepare_store` vs `complete_store`); when the request is finished **and** the last cascade `submit_store` has been issued, call `tier.on_request_finished`. Move the `reset_cache` finalize-on-abandon handling here too.
3. **Docstrings**: state the per-layer submission contract on both ABCs ("no more submits; completions / in-flight transfers may still occur").
4. **Test**: add a tiering-manager test asserting `tier.on_request_finished` fires only after the last cascade `submit_store`.

**Tradeoffs:** Cleaner, consistent contract that also frees the manager-level hook sooner. Cost is manager-side per-request lifecycle tracking plus handling the async-deferred last-block store. This is a refactor, deliberately kept out

issues.title: [Bug]: OTEL "Dynamo bytecode transform" span reports wildly incorrect duration (tens of thousands of days)
issues.body_head: ### 🐛 Describe the bug When OpenTelemetry tracing is enabled (`--otlp-traces-endpoint`), the `Dynamo bytecode transform` span emitted from `torch.compile` instrumentation reports a wildly incorrect duration — tens of thousands of days instead of the actual compile time (seconds). Example span observed in a trace backend: ``` Dynamo bytecode transform Service: llm Duration: 20622d 20h Start Time: 0μs (01:51:02.838) Kind: internal Status: unset Library Name: vllm.tracing.otel Span attributes dynamo.time_seconds 17.16094771400094 ``` The `dynamo.time_seconds` attribute (17.16s) is correct, but the span's own start/end timestamps used for the rendered `Duration` are off by ~56 years (~20622 days), which matches the gap between the Unix epoch and "now". ### Root cause In `vllm/compilation/backends.py` (around line 1145-1156): ```python from .monitor import torch_compile_start_time dynamo_time = time.perf_counter() - torch_compile_start_time ... start_time = int(torch_compile_start_time * 1e9) attributes = {"dynamo.time_seconds": dynamo_time} instrument_manual("Dynamo bytecode transform", start_time, None, attributes) ``` `torch_compile_start_time` is set in `vllm/compilation/monitor.py`: ```python torch_compile_start_time: float = 0.0 ... def ...(): global torch_compile_start_time torch_compile_start_time = time.perf_counter() ``` `time.perf_counter()` returns a value from a **monotonic clock with an arbitrary, implementation-defined reference point** (e.g. system boot time on Linux). It is only meaningful for measuring *elapsed* intervals via subtraction — it is **not** wall-clock/Unix-epoch time. However, `instrument_manual` forwards `start_time` directly into OpenTelemetry's `tracer.start_span(start_time=...)` (see `vllm/tracing/otel.py::manual_instrument_otel`), which expects **nanoseconds since the Unix epoch**: ```python span_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = { "name": span_name, "context": ctx, "start_time": start_time, } ... span = tracer.start_span(**span_kwargs) ... span.end() # end_time is None here, so OTel uses the real wall-clock "now" ``` Because `end_time` is `None`, `span.end()` stamps the end time using the real wall-clock `time.time_ns()`. So the span ends up with: - `start_time` ≈ `perf_counter()` value (small, interpreted as if it were close to the 1970 epoch) - `end_time` ≈ actu

issues.body_head:
Hi folks — during my testing on an MI355 (gfx950) box I went to run `test_rocm_mxfp4_moe_oracle` and found it's been quietly broken for a while. There's a top-level `ImportError` that makes pytest skip the whole test, so I don't think it's actually executed in a while, and a few API changes have drifted past it unnoticed. Once I patched the test back up to run, the `TRITON_UNFUSED` case passes but the plain fused `TRITON` case comes out with a ~90% mismatch against the reference, which I wanted to flag since I'm not sure if that's the test or the kernel.

Wanted to write it down before it gets lost.

### Environment

- AMD MI355 (gfx950), vLLM `0.23.1rc1.dev205+g0fbf42af8` (also reproduces on current `main`)
- torch `2.10.0` / HIP `7.2`, `amd-quark 0.11.2`, AITER available

### How to reproduce

```bash
pytest -v "tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py::test_rocm_mxfp4_moe_oracle"
```

### What I ran into

There are really two separate things here.

**1. The test is stale and doesn't run.** It dies at import, and once I got past that it turned out to be a small chain of drift that had piled up while the import error was hiding everything:

- `convert_to_mxfp4_moe_kernel_format` has been renamed to `convert_weight_to_mxfp4_moe_kernel_format`.
- `dynamic_mxfp4_quant` / `upcast_from_mxfp` are only imported at module scope under `if ROCM_AITER_AVAILABLE`, but the non-AITER `TRITON`/`TRITON_UNFUSED` cases use them, so you get a `NameError` when AITER is off.
- The kernel path calls `get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size()` with no TP group set up, so it hits `AssertionError: tensor model parallel group is not initialized` (a single-rank `dist_init` fixture sorts it out).
- `make_mxfp4_moe_kernel()` no longer takes the `shared_experts=` kwarg.

None of these are hard to fix — they're mechanical — but together they mean the test hasn't been doing anything.

**2. Once it runs, the fused `TRITON` case fails accuracy.** This is the part I'd really like a second opinion on:

```

AITER_MXFP4_BF16/FP8      -> SKIPPED (AITER off)
TRITON                    -> FAILED: Mismatch percentage is 0.8982 for rtol 0.3 (threshold: 0.0500)
```

`TRITON_UNFUSED` goes through the exact same harness and passes, so I don't think it's something I broke while fixing the test.

### My guess (could be wrong)

I lean towards this being a test-reference issue rather than a real kernel bug, because the production fused-TRITON path seems healthy — I ran a GPQA

issues.title: [Bug]: INCConfig doesn't support hybrid INT4+FP8 AutoRound checkpoints — weight_scale_inv params not loaded, model produces garbage output
issues.body_head:
**Describe the bug**

When loading a hybrid AutoRound checkpoint where expert FFN layers are INT4 (AutoGPTQ packing) and attention/shared-expert layers are FP8 (with per-block `weight_scale_inv` scales), vLLM loads the model without error but produces garbage output for every token.

The root cause is that `INCConfig` has no implementation of `maybe_update_config` — the base class stub is never overridden — so the quantizer never detects the FP8 layers in the checkpoint or registers their `weight_scale_inv` parameters. When the weight loader encounters those tensors it logs `Parameter X not found in params_dict, skip loading` for every attention layer, leaving scales uninitialized. Forward passes through all FP8 attention layers then produce garbage.

**Affected model**

`kleybrink/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Hybrid-INT4-FP8-MTP` (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B base with AutoRound hybrid quantization: INT4 MoE experts + FP8 attention / shared-expert layers with `weight_scale_inv` block scales).

Launched with `--quantization autoround` (which resolves to `quantization=inc`).

**To reproduce**

```bash
vllm serve kleybrink/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Hybrid-INT4-FP8-MTP \
  --quantization autoround \
  --max-model-len 8192
```

On startup you will see repeated warnings:
```
Parameter layers.N.linear_attn.in_proj_qkvz.weight_scale_inv not found in params_dict, skip loading
```
(one per attention layer per shard). All completions return garbage tokens.

**Expected behavior**

`INCConfig` should detect FP8 layers in the checkpoint (by scanning safetensors metadata for `float8_e4m3fn` weights that have a corresponding `weight_scale_inv` tensor), create an `Fp8Config` with the correct block size, and dispatch `Fp8LinearMethod` for those layers instead of `UnquantizedLinearMethod`.

**Fix**

Implement `maybe_update_config` on `INCConfig`. The logic:

1. Call `get_safetensors_params_metadata(model_name)` to inspect the checkpoint without loading weights.
2. Find all tensors with `dtype=float8_e4m3fn` that end in `.weight` and have a sibling `.weight_scale_inv` tensor — these are the FP8 layers.
3. Infer `weight_block_size` from the ratio of the weight shape to the scale shape.
4. Construct `Fp8Config(is_checkpoint_fp8_serialized=True, activation_scheme="dynamic", weight_block_size=...)` and store the set of FP8 layer prefixes.
5. In `apply_gptq_quant_layer` / `apply_awq_quant_layer`, when `get_layer_config` returns `weight_bits >= 16` (i.e., "not INT quantized"), check whether the layer is in the FP8 s

issues.title: [Bug][TurboQuant] Fast-path incorrectly triggers with continuation requests under prefix caching, losing cached prefix K/V
issues.body_head:
### Describe the bug

When using TurboQuant KV cache (`--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_*`) together with `--enable-prefix-caching`, the fast-path in `_prefill_attention` can trigger incorrectly on batches that contain both first-chunk prefills and continuation requests, causing continuation requests to **lose their cached prefix K/V** and produce hallucinated outputs.

### Root cause

In `vllm/v1/attention/backends/turboquant_attn.py`, the fast-path dispatch condition is:

```python
if _HAS_FLASH_ATTN and attn_metadata.max_query_len == attn_metadata.max_seq_len:
    return self._flash_attn_varlen(
        ...
        cu_seqlens_q=attn_metadata.query_start_loc,
        cu_seqlens_k=attn_metadata.query_start_loc,  # uses query_start_loc for K
        ...
    )
```

The assumption is that `max_query_len == max_seq_len` implies "no request has prior cached KV" (i.e., all requests are first-chunk prefills with `q_len == seq_len`). This is **incorrect**: a batch can contain a long first-chunk prefill (`q_len == seq_len = 1000`) alongside shorter continuation requests (`q_len = 100, seq_len = 500`, prefix cache hit). The max values still match (`1000 == 1000`), the fast-path fires, and `cu_seqlens_k=query_start_loc` causes continuation requests to attend only to their new tokens — **losing the cached prefix K/V entirely**.

### Reproduction

On C-Eval full (52 subjects) with `Qwen3-8B`, `turboquant_4bit_nc`, `--enable-prefix-caching`, `--max-num-seqs 512`:

| Config | Hallucinations |
|---|---|
| Prefix caching **OFF** | 0 |
| Prefix caching **ON**, full 52 subjects | **47–75** |
| Prefix caching **ON**, subset test | 0 |

The hallucinations appear only when:
1. TurboQuant KV cache is active
2. Prefix caching is enabled
3. Batch is diverse enough that `max_query_len == max_seq_len` holds despite continuation requests being present

### Proposed fix

Add a continuation guard computed from the already-populated CPU metadata fields (`query_start_loc_cpu`, `seq_lens_cpu` from PR #41434) — zero GPU sync cost:

```python
_has_continuation = False
if (attn_metadata.query_start_loc_cpu is not None
        and attn_metadata.seq_lens_cpu is not None):
    _qsl = attn_metadata.query_start_loc_cpu
    _sl = attn_metadata.seq_lens_cpu
    _has_continuation = (
        (_qsl[1:len(_sl) + 1] - _qsl[:len(_sl)]) != _sl
    ).any().item()

if (_HAS_FLASH_ATTN
        and attn_metadata.max_query_len == attn_metadata.max_seq_len
        and not _has_continuation):
    return self._flash

issues.title: [Bug]: Qwen3-VL video prompt expansion drops outer <|vision_start|>/<|vision_end|> wrapper, mismatching HuggingFace processor
issues.body_head:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

For **Qwen3-VL** video inputs, vLLM's multimodal prompt replacement produces a different `prompt_token_ids` sequence than the official HuggingFace `Qwen3VLProcessor`:

1. **2 fewer tokens** (e.g. 2065 vs 2067 in the token-only repro below).
2. **Different token order** at the start of the video block:
   - **HF (expected):** `...user\n<|vision_start|><0.3 seconds>...`
   - **vLLM (current):** `...user\n<0.3 seconds><|vision_start|>...`

The mismatch persists all the way into model `forward` — `prompt_token_ids` are not rewritten after the multimodal processor.

### Root cause

HuggingFace expands video in **two steps**:

1. The official Qwen3-VL chat template renders video as  
   `<|vision_start|><|video_pad|><|vision_end|>`  
   ([`Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct` `chat_template.json`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct/blob/main/chat_template.json)).

2. `Qwen3VLProcessor` only replaces the **inner** `<|video_pad|>` token via `get_text_with_replacements()`, keeping the outer wrapper intact  
   ([`processing_utils.py` L862–863, transformers `v5.12.0`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v5.12.0/src/transformers/processing_utils.py#L862-L863)).

3. `replace_video_token()` expands each frame as  
   `timestamp + <|vision_start|> + pad*N + <|vision_end|>`  
   ([`modular_qwen3_vl.py` L1137–1140, transformers `v5.12.0`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v5.12.0/src/transformers/models/qwen3_vl/modular_qwen3_vl.py#L1137-L1140)).

**Final HF sequence:**
```
<|vision_start|> + [per-frame: <t> + <|vision_start|> + pads + <|vision_end|>] + <|vision_end|>
```

In vLLM, **image** correctly replaces only `hf_processor.image_token` (`<|image_pad|>`), but **video** replaces the **entire** string  
`<|vision_start|><|video_pad|><|vision_end|>`  
with the per-frame expansion, which **consumes the outer wrapper**:

- Image target (correct): [`qwen3_vl.py` L1423, vLLM `v0.23.0`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.23.0/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_vl.py#L1423)
- Video target (bug): [`qwen3_vl.py` L1430, vLLM `v0.23.0`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.23.0/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_vl.py#L1430)
- `get_video_repl()` builds per-frame tokens without re-adding an outer wrapper: [`qwen3_vl.py` L1481–1486, vLLM `v0.23.0`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.23.0/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_vl.py#L1481-L1486)

This is inconsistent with both HuggingFace and vLLM's own image

text passes through as `content`. Conversely the JSON-oriented `llama3_json`

issues.title: [Bug]: Native MTP speculative decoding degenerates into garbage token loops on deep agentic conversations (Qwen3-MoE)
issues.body_head:
### Your current environment

<details>

- **vLLM:** v0.23.0
- **Model:** Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (BF16 and FP8)
- **GPU:** B300 GPU (single GPU, TP=1, DP=1).
- **dtype:** `torch.bfloat16`, `kv_cache_dtype=auto`.
- **Spec-decode:** `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'` (also seen at depth 3). The MTP draft module is the model's own MTP head (unquantized).
- **Sampling (client):** `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, no `top_k`, no repetition penalty, `max_tokens=20000`.

</details>


### 🐛 Describe the bug

### Expected

MTP spec-decode is a lossless acceleration: output distribution should match `speculative_config=None`. Right now, the output shows garbage output.

### Actual

On deep conversations, a fraction of turns collapse into a degenerate loop that runs to `max_tokens` and produces no usable output.

### Workaround

Disabling native MTP (`--speculative-config` removed) eliminates the degeneration. A repetition penalty / lower temperature might break the loops but was not validated.

### Reproducer

A minimal reproducer is provided here: 

[mtp_repro_minimal.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29521099/mtp_repro_minimal.zip)

Unmasked load of scales values interpreting 0xff as a NaN leading to NaN outputs. Root cause is in vendored third-party triton kernels (currently pinned to triton v3.5.1)

A potential fix in Triton v3.5.1: https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/0add68262ab0a2e33b84524346cb27cbb2787356/python/triton_kernels/triton_kernels/matmul_ogs_details/_matmul_ogs.py#L326-L327 (`vllm/third_party/triton_kernels/matmul_ogs_details/_matmul_ogs.py` in vLLM)
```
327,336c327
<                 if EVEN_K:
<                     hopper_scale_mask = tl.full([PACKED_MX_BLOCK], True, dtype=tl.int1)
<                 else:
<                     # PATCH: mask out the swizzled K tail.
<                     hopper_scale_mask = (offs_k_scale // 32) * MX_PACK_DIVISOR < k
<                 w_scales = unswizzle_mxfp4_scale_hopper(
<                     tl.load(WMxScalePtrs, mask=hopper_scale_mask[None, :], other=0),
<                     mx_axis=1,
<                     num_warps=num_warps,
<                 )
---
>                 w_scales = unswizzle_mxfp4_scale_hopper(tl.load(WMxScalePtrs), mx_axis=1, num_warps=num_warps)
```

Kernel Repro:
[repro_matmul_ogs.py](https://gist.github.com/yzong-rh/a42f1ef6161ed68c02c548b677cf31aa)
```
# FAILURE
.venv/bin/python repro_matmul_ogs.py

# NO FAILURE
FILL_VALUE=0xfe .venv/bin/python repro_matmul_ogs.py
FILL_VALUE=0x0 .venv/bin/python repro_matmul_ogs.py
```

### E2E Repro:

Apply patch: https://gist.github.com/yzong-rh/d4091b4fb37b9563099d81f218405824
- Allocates some memory and fill them with `0xff`. The memory is never used and should not change model output (but it does)

[eval_offline_harmony.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29557245/eval_offline_harmony.py)
```
# FAILURE: accuracy=0.0% (0/100), avg_output_len=256.0
python eval_offline_harmony.py 

# NO FAILURE: accuracy=100.0% (100/100), avg_output_len=29.0
FILL_VALUE=0xfe python eval_offline_harmony.py
FILL_VALUE=0 python eval_offline_harmony.py
```

Also breaks GSM8K and other benchmarks.

### Real World Failure Case:

`triton` is the default MXFP4 MoE backend for Hopper. Corrupted output can occur anytime some other operation allocates memory on GPU (allocating bitmasks for constrained decoding for example).

Encountered this while working on https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/4

issues.title: [Bug] NVFP4 flashinfer_b12x MoE produces empty/garbage output under pipeline or tensor parallel on SM120 — regression between dev552 (06-29) and dev601 (06-30)
issues.body_head:
**Title:** [Bug] NVFP4 `flashinfer_b12x` MoE produces empty/garbage output under pipeline or tensor parallel on SM120 — regression between dev552 (06-29) and dev601 (06-30)

## Summary

Serving `nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` with `--moe-backend=flashinfer_b12x` (SM120 native FP4 MoE, PR #40082) produces **empty completions or degenerate repeated-token output** (`<|box_end|>` spam) as soon as the model is sharded across 2 GPUs — with **either** `--pipeline-parallel-size=2` **or** `--tensor-parallel-size=2`. The identical config on a **single GPU** (no sharding) works correctly.

We bisected this to a **49-commit window between two daily nightly builds**:
- `0.23.1rc1.dev552+g4559c43a9` (2026-06-29) — **works correctly**
- `0.23.1rc1.dev601+ga16dbd5b8` (2026-06-30) — **broken**

Compare: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/compare/4559c43a9...a16dbd5b8

## Environment

- GPU: 2× NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti (16 GB), SM120 (Blackwell), no P2P between the two cards
- Driver: 610.43.02, CUDA 13.0 (torch 2.11.0+cu130)
- flashinfer-python: 0.6.12 (present in both the good dev552 and bad dev601/dev672 images — see note below)
- Docker images: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-<sha>` (official nightly builds)
- Model: `nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` (ModelOpt `MIXED_PRECISION`: W4A16_NVFP4 experts + FP8 attn/KV, hybrid GDN/Mamba + attention, 256 experts / 8 active)

## Command used (identical across every test below)

```
vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 \
  --served-model-name qwen3.6-moe-nvfp4 --trust-remote-code \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_b12x --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-model-len 131072 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
  --max-num-seqs 8 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8005
```
(`flashinfer_b12x` correctly selected in all runs — confirmed via log line `Using 'FLASHINFER_B12X' NvFp4 MoE backend`. Attention backend auto-selects `FLASHINFER`.)

## Symptom

```
$ curl .../v1/completions -d '{"prompt":"The capital of France is","max_tokens":12,"temperature":0}'
{"choices":[{"text":""}]}          # on broken builds: empty
```
or, via chat completions:
```
"content": "<|box_end|><|box_end|><|box_end|>...<|box_end|>"   # repeated to max_tokens
```
No errors, warnings, or NaNs are logged. The server reports healthy and serves requests normally (200 OK) — the failure is purely in generation quality.

## Bisection (9 daily nightly images, 2026-06-22 → 2026-07-01)

| D

issues.title: [Feature]: Detect CUDA toolchain/driver PTX version mismatch at startup and raise an actionable error
issues.body_head:
## Feature request

Detect a CUDA-toolkit-vs-driver PTX version mismatch at startup and raise a clear, actionable error instead of letting it surface as an opaque `cudaErrorUnsupportedPtxVersion` deep in a kernel launch stack trace.

## Motivation

Hit this on a from-source build for NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark, sm_121): built with nvcc 13.3, but the installed driver (580.159.03) only supports CUDA 13.0 PTX JIT. `_vllm_fa2_C` has no native sm_121 cubin (sm_80 baseline only), so it falls back to PTX JIT at runtime — and the driver rejects PTX from a toolchain newer than it supports. The crash only happens for models whose attention-backend oracle picks `FLASH_ATTN` (plain bf16/GQA models); NVFP4/quantized models that route to `FLASHINFER` never touch the affected code path, so the failure looks intermittent/model-specific even though the root cause is a build-environment property, not a model property.

The actual error gives no hint about the real cause:
```
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: the provided PTX was compiled with an unsupported toolchain.
cudaErrorUnsupportedPtxVersion
```
A user hitting this has to independently discover that (a) it's PTX JIT, not a native cubin, (b) the specific op involved has no native cubin for their SM, and (c) their nvcc/driver versions are skewed — none of which is stated anywhere in the trace.

Same underlying gap shows up in #38411 (SM100/Jetson Thor, `_vllm_fa2_C` compiled SM80-only, no override for the vision encoder path) and the general error class in #31027 and #36234/#36235 — different GPUs/toolchains, same missing diagnostic.

## Proposed change

At engine startup (or lazily, the first time a PTX-JIT fallback path is about to be hit), compare the CUDA version embedded in vLLM's compiled extensions against `torch.cuda.get_device_properties`/driver-reported max-supported CUDA version, and if the build toolchain is newer than what the driver can JIT, fail fast with a message like:

```
vLLM was built with CUDA 13.3, but the installed driver (580.159.03) only
supports CUDA 13.0 for runtime PTX compilation. Kernel `_vllm_fa2_C` has no
native cubin for your GPU (sm_121) and requires PTX JIT, which will fail.
Fix: update your driver, rebuild vLLM against CUDA <=13.0, or pass
--attention-backend flashinfer/TRITON_ATTN to avoid this kernel.
```

rather than letting it surface as a raw `cudaErrorUnsupportedPtxVersion` several frames deep in CUDA graph capture.

## Alternatives considered

- Just document `--attention-backe

issues.title: [Bug][XPU] compressed-tensors FP8 W8A8 (dynamic) generates garbage output on Intel Arc Pro B70 (Battlemage)
issues.body_head:
### Your current environment
Environment (vllm collect_env, abridged) ``` vLLM version : 0.23.1rc1.dev920+gdd127d82e (main @ dd127d82), VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=xpu PyTorch version : 2.12.0+xpu (XPU build 20250302) Python version : 3.12.3, glibc 2.39, Linux 7.0.0 x86_64 Intel GPU : Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B70 Graphics (Battlemage / Xe2), 32 GB Level Zero driver : 26.18.38308.1-0 Intel Graphics Compiler : 2.34.4 oneAPI compiler : 2025.3.3 vllm-xpu-kernels : 0.1.10.1 triton-xpu : 3.7.1 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Serving a **compressed-tensors FP8 W8A8** checkpoint (8-bit per-channel weights, 8-bit **dynamic per-token** activations, `float-quantized` format) on the **XPU backend** loads without error but produces garbage tokens under greedy decoding. Reproduced with an **unmodified, official, widely-used checkpoint**, so this is not a checkpoint problem — it points at the XPU FP8 linear path. **Minimal repro (stock model, no custom code):** ```bash vllm serve RedHatAI/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-FP8-dynamic \ --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 4096 --enforce-eager # Intel Arc Pro B70 (Battlemage), XPU backend ``` Greedy (`temperature=0`) generations: - Prompt `The capital of France is` → `' ,ricsmalink빌 * 若要 ?");\n...">\n******\n\n"syncurrenc！"...'` - Prompt `Write one sentence about the ocean.` → `'".\n\n\n\n".\n\n\n\n%);\n... 若要="#">...'` The same checkpoint generates correctly on CUDA. **Independent isolation** (a second model, Qwen3.5-MoE, our own quant): bf16 weights + int4 experts generate correctly; introducing FP8 on *any* linear (all linears, or `self_attn` only) reproduces the garbage. So the failure tracks the FP8 linear kernel, independent of model/architecture. Failing checkpoint's quant config group: ``` weights: {num_bits: 8, type: float, strategy: channel, symmetric: true} input_activations: {num_bits: 8, type: float, strategy: token, dynamic: true} format: float-quantized ``` This looks like a numerics bug in the XPU `scaled_mm` FP8 path (the W8A8 kernel added in #43645). A Battlemage numerics unit test against a reference GEMM would catch it. Happy to test patches or provide more traces. Searched existing issues — no XPU FP8 correctness report found.

issues.title: [Bug]: xpu_mla_sparse NaN-poisons attention output when a row's leading topk index chunk is fully masked
issues.body_head:
### Your current environment

The defect is in device-agnostic Triton source (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/xpu_mla_sparse.py`), analyzed on vLLM main @ `54503ec`. Reproduced with Triton 3.7.1 — the repro below runs on any GPU, and even under `TRITON_INTERPRET=1` on CPU, since it is a pure numerics bug, not a device one.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`_bf16_mla_sparse_kernel` NaN-poisons its output whenever the **first `BLOCK_N` (=16) topk index entries of a row are all masked** (`-1` padding or `>= seq_kv`), even though valid keys follow later in the index list.

**Mechanism** (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/xpu_mla_sparse.py`):

- L76: the running max starts at `-inf`: `e_max = tl.zeros([BLOCK_H], dtype=tl.float32) - float("inf")`
- L125: a fully-masked chunk sets every logit to `-inf`: `qk = tl.where(mask, qk, -float("inf"))`
- L139–141:
  ```python
  n_e_max = tl.maximum(tl.max(qk, 1), e_max)   # max(-inf, -inf) = -inf
  re_scale = tl.exp2(e_max - n_e_max)          # exp2(-inf - -inf) = exp2(nan) = nan
  p = tl.exp2(qk - n_e_max[:, None])           # nan
  ```
  `acc *= re_scale` and `e_sum = e_sum * re_scale + tl.sum(p, 1)` are then permanently poisoned — `nan × 0 = nan`, so no later valid chunk can rescue the accumulator. The NaNs flow silently into the attention output.

A row with **no valid key at all** likewise returns NaN (`0/0` at the epilogue), where the in-tree reference (`reference_mla_sparse_prefill` in `tests/kernels/attention/test_xpu_mla_sparse.py`, L67–69) explicitly defines the output of such rows as **zeros**.

**Blast radius** — every caller of `triton_bf16_mla_sparse_interface`:
- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/xpu_mla_sparse.py` L219 (XPU_MLA_SPARSE backend forward)
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/xpu/xpu_sparse.py` L342 (DSA prefill)
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/xpu/xpu_sparse_decode_fp8.py` L282 (fp8 decode wrapper)

**Why the existing test doesn't catch it:** `test_bf16_triton_sparse_mla` writes valid indices at the *front* of each row and pads with `-1` at the *back* (L98–102), so a leading chunk is never fully masked. Trailing padding is benign (by then `e_max` is finite). The newer sparse-MLA kernel from #47629 already avoids this exact pattern with a finite sentinel; this kernel predates that.

### Minimal repro

```python
# Run on any GPU; runs on CPU too via the Triton interpreter (auto-enabled).
import os
import torch
if not torch.cuda.is_available():
    os.environ["TRITON_INTERPRET"] = "1"
from vllm.v1.attention.ops.xpu_mla_sparse import triton_

### Your current environment

### 🐛 Describe the bug

After upgrading vLLM from 0.24.0 to 0.25.0, openbmb/MiniCPM-V-4.6 can no longer be served. The same local model files and launch command work correctly with vLLM 0.24.0.
vLLM fails while loading the safetensors checkpoint with the following error:

````python
ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'qkqkv_proj' in MiniCPMV4_6ViTWindowAttentionSelfAttn. 
The available parameters belonging to  (MiniCPMV4_6ViTWindowAttentionSelfAttn) are: {'qkv_proj.bias', 'out_proj.bias', 'qkv_proj.weight', 'out_proj.weight'}
````

It appears that the vision attention weight named qkv_proj is incorrectly processed by the packed-module mapping for q_proj, k_proj, and v_proj. Since qkv_proj ends with v_proj, it may be mistakenly rewritten to qkqkv_proj.
This happens during checkpoint loading, before the server starts accepting requests. It does not appear to be related to GPU memory settings, context length, or the custom chat template.

Launch command:

````python
vllm serve --model /mnt/e/models/MiniCPM-V-4.6 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --port 8000 \
  --max-model-len 10240 
````

issues.title: [Bug]: #47327 dense-MHA split breaks FlashMLA sparse: OOB write in top-k index conversion, corrupted fp8_ds_mla context gather
issues.body_head:
### Summary

#47327 (`c4f5cd60d`, "[1/N] Add dense MHA path for sparse MLA short sequences") routes short prefills (`prefill_max_seq_len <= topk_tokens`) to a dense-MHA path, so `forward_mqa` now receives only the leading `num_decode_tokens` tokens of the batch instead of all of them. Two parts of the FlashMLA sparse backend were not updated for that new contract:

1. an **out-of-bounds write** in the top-k index conversion whenever the split is active (any kv-cache dtype);
2. the dense-MHA path gathers cached context in a way that does not understand the **`fp8_ds_mla`** cache layout — silently wrong K/V without DCP, hard error with DCP.

Both are regressions from #47327: before it, every token went through the MQA path. cc @MatthewBonanni

### Repro

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla
```

**Bug 1 (OOB).** Send concurrent traffic so that a scheduler step holds at least one running decode plus a new short prompt (total seq len ≤ `index_topk` = 2048). The dense-MHA split activates, `forward_mqa` gets only the decode tokens, and the index-conversion kernel writes past the end of its output buffer: non-deterministic corruption of neighbouring GPU allocations, or `CUDA error: an illegal memory access`. Also reproduces with `--kv-cache-dtype auto` (bf16 cache).

**Bug 2 (context gather).** Multi-turn chat or any prefix-cache hit, i.e. a prefill that arrives with computed context, total sequence ≤ 2048. Without DCP the request completes but its context K/V is garbage, so the output is silently wrong. With DCP it raises `RuntimeError: src_cache and dst must have the same dtype`.

### Root cause 1 — unsliced `req_id_per_token`

`FlashMLASparseImpl.forward_mqa` slices `topk_indices = self.topk_indices_buffer[:num_actual_toks]` with `num_actual_toks = q.shape[0]` (the MQA subset), but all three forward paths pass the **full-batch** `attn_metadata.req_id_per_token` to `triton_convert_req_index_to_global_index`:

- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashmla_sparse.py:602` (`_forward_bf16_kv`), `:643` (`_forward_fp8_kv_separate_prefill_decode`), `:741` (`_forward_fp8_kv_mixed_batch`)

The converter sizes its grid by `req_id.shape[0]` but allocates `out = torch.empty_like(token_indices)` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_utils.py:168,176`), so rows `[num_mqa_tokens, num_batch_tokens)` are written **past the end of `out`**.

issues.title: [Bug] enable_lora on hybrid-MoE model perturbs outputs of requests WITHOUT lora_request (greedy repetition loop) — fused MoE LoRA implementation
issues.body_head:
**Summary**: With a hybrid-attention MoE model (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, W4A16 compressed-tensors) and `enable_lora=True`, greedy generations for requests **without** any `lora_request` differ from the same checkpoint served with `enable_lora=False` — badly enough to flip a fluent completion into a degenerate repetition loop. Startup logs show `MoE model detected. Using fused MoE LoRA implementation.`, which suggests the LoRA-enabled fused-MoE path is not numerically neutral for non-LoRA requests.

**Environment**: vllm 0.24.0+cu129, 1×L40S (SM8.9), CUDA 12.4 (driver 550). Model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B quantized to W4A16 (compressed-tensors, per-expert layout) + FP8 KV cache.

**Repro**:

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
llm = LLM(model=CKPT, max_model_len=4096, gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,
          enable_lora=True, max_lora_rank=64, kv_cache_dtype="fp8", max_num_seqs=64)
out = llm.generate(["The capital of France is"], SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=48))
```

- `enable_lora=True`, no lora_request → `" Paris.\nThe capital of France is Paris.\nThe capital of France is Paris.\n..."` (repetition loop)
- `enable_lora=False`, same ckpt/params → `" Paris, a city renowned for its iconic landmarks such as the Eiffel Tower, ..."` (fluent)
- Applying a trained LoRA adapter via `lora_request` on the LoRA-enabled engine also produces fluent output — only the **no-adapter path under enable_lora** is degraded.

**Expected**: requests without `lora_request` should be numerically identical (or indistinguishable) regardless of `enable_lora`.

**Impact**: base-vs-adapter A/B comparisons on one engine are unreliable for hybrid-MoE models; greedy no-adapter traffic can degenerate on a LoRA-enabled server.

issues.title: [Bug]: MiniMax-M3 NVFP4 produces garbage output + CUDA illegal memory access on Hopper (sm90) via Marlin FP4-MoE
issues.body_head:
### Summary

Serving **MiniMax-M3-NVFP4** on **Hopper GPUs (H100 / H200, sm90)** loads and starts the server, but the FP4-MoE forward pass is broken in two independent ways:

1. **Incoherent output** — every request returns garbage (null bytes / repeated-token soup) instead of real text, even at concurrency 1.
2. **CUDA illegal memory access** — the engine crashes at concurrency ≈ 8 inside `fused_marlin_moe`, killing the worker (`EngineDeadError`).

Both reproduce on the **v0.25.1 release** and on the current **nightly**. On Hopper the NVFP4-MoE selector falls back to **MARLIN** (the FlashInfer FP4 backends are Blackwell/SM100-only), and the Marlin FP4-MoE path is where both failures originate.

### Environment

- GPU: **NVIDIA H200** and **H100** (Hopper, sm90)

issues.title: [Bug]: Streaming vs non-streaming content whitespace mismatch at tool-call boundaries (ParserEngine: qwen3/nemotron_v3/seed_oss/glm47_moe/gemma4)
issues.body_head:
### Description

For engine-based parsers, streaming and non-streaming produce **different `content`** for the same model output when plain text sits immediately before, between, or after a tool call.

The non-streaming path strips whitespace from tool-associated content (`_strip_content_whitespace` → `content.strip()` in `vllm/parser/engine/parser_engine.py`, gated by config flag `strip_content_whitespace_with_tools`, default `True`). The streaming path (`extract_tool_calls_streaming` / `parse_delta` → `_events_to_delta` → `_strip_trailing_reasoning`) has no equivalent step for `delta.content` — `_strip_trailing_reasoning` only trims `delta.reasoning`, and `_events_to_delta`'s own whitespace handling only covers content that is *entirely* whitespace before the first non-whitespace chunk arrives. Boundary whitespace on real (non-whitespace) content adjacent to a tool call is never stripped in streaming.

This is not just a synthetic edge case: BPE tokenizers commonly fuse a leading space onto the following word as one token. Verified against the real Qwen3 tokenizer:

```python
>>> from transformers import AutoTokenizer
>>> tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3-8B")
>>> tok.encode(" done.")
[2814, 13]
>>> [tok.decode([i]) for i in tok.encode(" done.")]
[' done', '.']
```

So `" done"` is genuinely emitted as a single token in a real streaming response — this triggers whenever a model emits any prose right before/after a tool call, which is a very common pattern (e.g. "Let me check that for you. `<tool_call>...`").

### Reproduction

Environment: offline, no GPU/torch build needed — the parser engine is pure Python. Repro script feeds identical model output through the real streaming path (`extract_tool_calls_streaming`, token-by-token) and the real non-streaming path (`extract_tool_calls`), then diffs `content`.

Minimal case (Qwen3, `enable_thinking=False` so pre/post-tool text is `content` not `reasoning`):

```python
model_output = (
    "<tool_call>\n<function=get_weather>\n"
    "<parameter=location>Paris</parameter>\n</function>\n</tool_call>"
    " done."
)
# fed through streaming as real BPE-like tokens: [..., ' done', '.']

non_streaming_content = "done."
streaming_content     = " done."   # <-- leading space leaks through
```

Also reproduces for text *between* two parallel tool calls (non-streaming: `"mid"`, streaming: `"mid "` or `" mid "` depending on chunking) and for text *before* the first tool call, on parsers whose initial state

issues.title: [Bug]: MTP draft model ignores checkpoint per-layer quantization config (block_name_to_quantize mapped inconsistently vs target)
issues.body_head:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment</summary>

```text
Resolution logic inspected on vllm-project/vllm main @ f83de6d (2026-07-23).
Behavior originally observed on a 0.23.1 nightly derivative (eugr/spark-vllm,
2026-07-20) serving Qwen3.5-122B-A10B (INC/AutoRound checkpoint) on GB10 / DGX Spark.
This is a pure-python config-resolution defect; it is not hardware-specific.
```
</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

An MTP (multi-token-prediction) speculative-decoding **draft** model can never load quantized weights for its decoder layers from the checkpoint, even when the checkpoint ships properly formatted quantized MTP tensors and marks them as quantized. The per-layer quantization config is resolved **inconsistently** for the draft model vs the target model, so every MTP layer silently falls back to an Unquantized method.

#### Resolution chain (cites on current `main` @ `f83de6d`)

1. **INC/AutoRound checkpoints mark quantized layers by prefix.**
   `INCConfigParser` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/inc/config_parser.py:146-150`:
   ```python
   if self._config.block_name_to_quantize:
       quantized = any(
           layer_name.startswith(name)
           for name in self._config.block_name_to_quantize
       )
   ```
   `layer_name` here is the **vLLM runtime** module name.

2. **`block_name_to_quantize` is mapped from HF names to vLLM names only for model classes that expose `hf_to_vllm_mapper`.**
   `configure_quant_config` in `vllm/model_executor/model_loader/utils.py:291-312`:
   ```python
   if not issubclass(model_class, SupportsQuant):
       hf_to_vllm_mapper = getattr(model_class, "hf_to_vllm_mapper", None)
       ...
       if hf_to_vllm_mapper is not None:
           quant_config.apply_vllm_mapper(hf_to_vllm_mapper.get_unstacked_mapper())
   ```
   For INC, `apply_vllm_mapper` rewrites `block_name_to_quantize` (`inc/inc.py:139-146`).

3. **The target model class exposes a mapper; the registered MTP draft class does not.**
   - Target `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` (`models/qwen3_5.py:399`) inherits `hf_to_vllm_mapper` from `Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration` (`models/qwen3_vl.py:1705`) → block names get mapped to vLLM space.

issues.title: [Bug]: DeepGemm accuracy auto-disable (_DEEPGEMM_BLACKWELL_EXCLUDED_MODEL_TYPES) does not apply to the FP8 MoE path
issues.body_head:
### Your current environment

- Hardware: NVIDIA GB10, **SM121 / compute capability 12.1** (also relevant to SM120 generally)
- vLLM **0.26.0** (standard PyPI wheel, aarch64), torch 2.11.0+cu130, `--enforce-eager`, TP=1
- Model: `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` — `model_type: **qwen3_5_moe_text**`, 256-expert FP8 MoE

### 🐛 Describe the bug

vLLM correctly identifies that DeepGemm is inaccurate for this model type and logs so at startup:

```
WARNING [vllm.py:1008] Auto-disabled DeepGemm for model_type=qwen3_5_moe_text on Blackwell.
  DeepGemm E8M0 scale format causes accuracy degradation for this architecture.
  Falling back to CUTLASS. To disable DeepGemm globally, set VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0.
```

…and then **selects DeepGemm anyway for the MoE layers**:

```
INFO [fp8.py:405] Using DEEPGEMM Fp8 MoE backend out of potential backends:
  ['AITER', 'FLASHINFER_TRTLLM', 'FLASHINFER_CUTLASS', 'DEEPGEMM', 'TRITON', 'MARLIN', ...]
```

The auto-disable sets `quant_config.use_deep_gemm = False` (`vllm/config/vllm.py`), and
`qwen3_5_moe_text` **is** present in `_DEEPGEMM_BLACKWELL_EXCLUDED_MODEL_TYPES`
(`vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py`) — so the denylist is doing its job. But `use_deep_gemm` appears to have
**no references anywhere under `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/`**; the FP8 MoE backend
selector honors only the `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM` / `VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM` env vars. Net effect: the
denylist covers dense linear layers only, and the MoE layers — where the accuracy concern for an MoE
model actually matters most — still run DeepGemm.

So the warning is truthful about dense layers and silently wrong about MoE.

### Why this surfaced now

**PR #43477** ("Enable DeepSeek V4 and GLM-5.1 on SM120", shipped v0.24.0) added
`is_device_capability_family(120)` to `deep_gemm.py`. Prior to that, the SM100-family gate meant
DeepGemm was never *eligible* on SM121, so this gap was latent. The FP8 MoE backend priority list
itself is unchanged — DeepGemm simply became eligible and started winning.

Consistent with this, the original accuracy fix **#37804** reasoned that "MoE layers are unaffected
(already use FLASHINFER_TRTLLM)" — which holds on SM100 but **not** on SM121, where
FLASHINFER_TRTLLM is gated out (#43906).

### Impact

1. **Accuracy** — the exact degradation #37804 set out to prevent still applies to this model's MoE
   layers on SM120/121.
2. **Performance** — measurable on our hardware. Forcing Triton MoE (matching what vLLM 0.20.1
   selected) recovered most of a regressi

## Summary

GSM8K accuracy drops ~5 percentage points when moving from `vllm/vllm-openai:latest` (v0.26.0) to `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` on the same cluster, same config, same benchmark command.

## GSM8K Results

### Setup

- **Benchmark**: [GSM8K](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/gsm8k) (grade school math, 1319 test examples)
- **Evaluator**: `lm_eval` v0.4.x, `local-chat-completions` model type
- **Few-shot**: 5-shot (`fewshot_as_multiturn=True`, default for chat completions)
- **Thinking**: Disabled (`enable_thinking: false` via `chat_template_kwargs`)
- **Sampling**: Greedy (`temperature=0.0`, `do_sample=False`)
- **Stop tokens**: `['Question:', '</s>', '<|im_end|>']`
- **Tokenizer**: HuggingFace backend

### Raw results

**`vllm/vllm-openai:latest`** (v0.26.0, commit [`ffd46bfab`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ffd46bfab2128bb84146050e98b51a617c6575ab)):

|-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:|
|gsm8k|      3|flexible-extract|     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9447|±  |0.0063|
|     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9386|±  |0.0066|
```

Tested across concurrency 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384 — all consistently ~94.5%.

**`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`** (0.26.1rc1.dev77, commit [`6f91edf96`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/6f91edf96d3f3272945809c04702380053bff4de)):

|-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:|

|     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  |0.8855|±  |0.0088|
```

At 512 concurrency. 377 commits between the two versions.

### Regression summary

| Metric | latest (0.26.0) | nightly (0.26.1rc1.dev77) | Delta |
|--------|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| flexible-extract | 94.47% ± 0.63 | 89.31% ± 0.85 | **−5.16%** |
| strict-match | 93.86% ± 0.66 | 88.55% ± 0.88 | **−5.31%** |

```

- **Hardware**: 2× NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark), one GPU per node, 2-node cluster joined via Ray (TCP/RoCE interconnect)

Switching to the default loader (removing the flag entirely) with an otherwise-identical launch command produces fluent, well-formed text for the same prompt and sampling parameters.

  --block-size 256 \

issues.title: [Bug]: expanded_block_table_buffer width mismatch in the DSA indexer under DCP
issues.body_head:
### Your current environment

GLM-5.2, TP8, `--decode-context-parallel-size 2`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, MTP. Reported by @Leoyzen on 0.26.1rc1 (post-#50302): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50302#issuecomment-5161430855

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Decode crashes in `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`:

```
RuntimeError: The expanded size of the tensor (8192) must match the existing size (16384)
at non-singleton dimension 1.  Target sizes: [30, 8192].  Tensor sizes: [30, 16384]
```

`UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` does not override `max_num_blocks_per_req`, so it falls back to `cdiv(max_len, block_size)` while `AttentionSpec` divides by `decode_context_parallel_size`. The runner sizes the block table from the group spec (`may_reinitialize_input_batch`), the metadata builders are constructed from the per-layer spec (`create_metadata_builders`), so under DCP the block table is `dcp_world_size` times wider than the indexer's buffer. DSA models are affected because their indexer and MLA layers merge into one uniform-type group.

Predates #50302 and is a separate issue from the alignment it fixed. The new `gpu/model_runner.py` divides by `dcp_size` explicitly and is not affected. Same symptom, different causes: #46794 (InputBatch not rebuilt after `max_model_len` is auto-reduced), #43970 (alignment, superseded by #50302).

Fix: #50823.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the docs chatbot in the [vLLM documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/) for help.

issues.title: [Bug]: MiniMax-M3 fp8 KV cache on SM80 (A100/A800): coherent with --enforce-eager, garbage under CUDA graphs — root cause + working fix
issues.body_head:
### Your current environment

- 8x A800-80GB (SM80, no native fp8 tensor cores), TP=8
- Model: MiniMax-M3-AWQ-INT4 (weight-only int4)
- Launch: `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e5m2 --max-model-len 1048576 --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --block-size 128 --enable-chunked-prefill`
- Findings below were made on a community M3 fork; mainline shares the `_insert_kv` KV-write path this report is about. Full container env available on request.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Trying to run MiniMax-M3 with an fp8 KV cache on A100/A800 fails two different ways:

1. `fp8` (e4m3): Triton refuses outright — `type fp8e4nv not supported in this architecture`. SM80 can only read `fp8_e5m2` (same conclusion as #3965).
2. `fp8_e5m2`: the server boots, takes a 1M-token window, and generates pure garbage.

The garbage is **not** an fp8 precision problem. We measured the e5m2 write/read kernels on SM80 directly: round-trip error 4.5%, full-kernel 12–16% — normal for a 2-mantissa-bit format. The decisive experiment:

- `--enforce-eager`: output is perfectly coherent (but 5.2 tok/s — unusable for an 8-TP MoE);
- any CUDA-graph mode: garbage.

Root cause: the bf16 path writes KV through a fused CUDA op, which is graph-safe. The fp8 path goes through `MiniMaxM3SparseAttention._insert_kv` — plain Python that allocates a fresh tensor and does an advanced-index scatter (`idx_cache[slot_mapping] = ...`). Under graph capture that write corrupts the index-K cache, the sparse indexer picks the wrong top-k blocks, and attention reads the wrong KV. This one mechanism explains all three observations (bf16+graph fine, fp8+graph garbage, fp8+eager fine).

Fix that works: decorate `_insert_kv` with `@eager_break_during_capture` (the codebase's own idiom for exactly this), route dense-layer KV writes through the CUDA `reshape_and_cache_flash` (software fp8 convert), and relax the SM89 guards to SM80. With that, on 8xA800:

- full 1,048,576-token window fits (fp8 halves KV; pool ~1.22M tokens);
- coherent output; needle retrieval hit at ~100k depth; an 840k-token prompt prefills clean;
- ~86 tok/s decode, ≈90% of the bf16 baseline — on SM80 fp8-KV buys memory, not speed;

issues.title: [Bug]: EngineCore dies on first guided-decoding request when dspark speculative decoding is enabled (grammar bitmask width mismatch)

## Summary

With `--speculative-config.method=dspark` enabled on `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, the **first request that uses guided decoding** (`response_format={"type": "json_object"}`, JSON schema, or enforced `tool_choice`) crashes the EngineCore:

```
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (4040) must match the size of tensor b (4041) at non-singleton dimension 1
```

The whole engine dies: every in-flight and subsequent request returns 500 until the engine finishes a multi-minute restart (model reload + warmup + draft-module setup). A single malformed-width bitmask should never be fatal to the engine.

The identical configuration **without** the speculative config serves guided decoding correctly, so the over-wide bitmask is produced only on the speculative-decode scheduler path.

- vLLM `0.26.0` (official Docker image `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.26.0`)
- torch `2.11.0+cu130`, CUDA 13.0, FlashInfer `0.6.14`, Triton `3.6.0`
- 4× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120, 96 GB), single node, TP=4
- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (vocab_size = 129,280), which ships its DSpark draft module in-checkpoint
- Structured outputs backend: `guidance`

Note on hardware: running this fp8 model on SM120 with the stock v0.26.0 wheel required four small local workarounds in GEMM/attention kernel dispatch (listed in the appendix — they are themselves upstream gaps). None of them touch the scheduler, speculative decoding, structured outputs, or sampling code, so they cannot cause the bug reported here. On SM90/SM100 the model should run without any of them.

issues.title: [Model] Kimi-K3: all requests degenerate to a repeated token after long-context prefill (NaN logits; packed KDA prefill suspected)
issues.body_head:
# Summary

Serving `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` at long context reproducibly degenerates: once a large-context request (~240K tokens, well inside the model's 1M-token spec) is processed, the deployment begins returning a **single repeated degenerate token on every step for every subsequent request**, never samples EOS, and every request runs to `max_tokens`. In the observed incident the state persisted ~19 hours and the set of corrupted requests grew over time (2 → 8 concurrent), i.e. the corruption **spreads between requests and is permanent per request** until process restart.

We have proven the logits go NaN (see below); what remains open is *where* the NaN originates. This issue is filed as an investigation-in-progress with the evidence, two ready-to-run repro tests, and a concrete suspect code path — AI assistance was used in the investigation and in preparing this report.

# Proven mechanism (established from the live system, not inferred)

- The emitted token id is **0** every step. `KimiK3Config` sets `pad_token_id = 0`; chat deltas render empty (special token skipped) while `/v1/completions` renders ` @`.
- Constant index-0 output means `greedy_sample` (`vllm/v1/sample/sampler.py:240`) returned argmax over NaN logits (argmax over NaN resolves to index 0).
- Confirming evidence: while debugging, a logprobs request against this deployment killed the (Rust) frontend with `token_ranks must be >= 1 for decoded engine-core logprobs`. The rank is computed as `(logprobs >= sampled_logprob).sum(-1)`; that count can only be 0 when the sampled logprob is NaN (all IEEE-754 comparisons against NaN are false).

# Environment

- Image `vllm/vllm-openai:kimi-k3`, `max_model_len=256000`
- `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, `VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1`, `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`
- Prefix-cache hit rate measured 0.0% throughout the incident
- (A `collect_env.py` re-run from the affected pod is pending; happy to attach.)

# Why this looks like an implementation bug, not a model limit

- 240K ≪ the 1M context window in the K3 tech report.
- The vLLM K3 port is very new (~7 commits in `vllm/models/kimi_k3/`; `kda.py` has two) and is registered outside `vllm.model_executor.models` (`registry.py:466`), the shape of an in-progress vendor drop (`[Model] Add Kimi K3 support: model files and kernels [1/N]`).
- `VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1` bypassed the usual length guard.

# Hypotheses checked and eliminated

| Candidate | Verdict |

| Stale KDA state-slot reuse | **R

issues.title: [Bug]: OffloadingConnector can silently return wrong output at exact chunk boundaries with mamba_cache_mode=all
issues.body_head:
### Your current environment

Reproduced with:

- vLLM: `0.25.1` nightly, commit `752a3a504`
- Model: `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2` (hybrid full-attention + Mamba)
- `enable_prefix_caching=True`
- `mamba_cache_mode="all"` (the model's default when prefix caching is enabled)
- `OffloadingConnector`, CPU KV offload enabled
- eager execution, greedy decoding

The relevant condition is still present in v0.26.0 and current `main` (`43c4bdcae9e589fde99984d1d5d03cbdeecf716b` as checked on 2026-08-05), although I have not rerun the GPU reproduction on those revisions yet.

### Describe the bug

`OffloadingConnector` can silently produce different output after a CPU-cache refetch when the prompt length is exactly a multiple of the offloaded Mamba chunk size and `mamba_cache_mode="all"`.

`resolve_mamba_align_size()` currently enables hit-window alignment only for `mamba_cache_mode == "align"`:

```python
if isinstance(kv_spec, MambaSpec) and kv_spec.mamba_cache_mode == "align":
    ...
```

However, `"all"` mode also stores recurrent Mamba states at token/block positions. A prefix lookup is capped at `num_tokens - 1` because the final token must be recomputed for logits. At an exact chunk boundary, without alignment the offload lookup can therefore return `N - 1` tokens while restoring the state stored at boundary `N`. That state already contains token `N`, so recomputing token `N` from it applies the token twice and changes the output without raising an exception.

### Reproduction

1. Create an `LLM` with the configuration above.
2. Use a deterministic token prompt whose length is exactly two offload chunks. In this model/configuration the chunk size was 1408 tokens, so the prompt length was 2816.
3. Generate once with greedy decoding to populate the CPU offload cache.
4. Clear the GPU prefix cache while retaining the connector cache (`reset_connector=False`; on the tested revision the default reset retained it).
5. Generate the identical prompt again.

Observed:

```text
cold:    prompt=2816 cached=0    first tokens=[18631, 43085, 17091, 47695, 1556]
refetch: prompt=2816 cached=2815 first tokens=[18631, 43085, 17091, 47695, 1270]
```

The engine completes normally, but the fifth generated token differs.

With the one-line change below, the refetch is rounded back to a valid recurrent-state boundary (`cached=1408` in this setup) and the generated output is bitwise identical to the cold run:

```diff

issues.title: [Bug]: Step3p5ReasoningParser strips the wrong newline once the discarded prefix is preserved (follow-up to #50918)
issues.body_head:
### Your current environment

Code-level report against `main`; no runtime environment required. The affected
path is pure Python string handling.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**This is a latent issue: it does not reproduce on `main` today.** It becomes
real once #50918 merges. Anyone testing current `main` will correctly see nothing
wrong, so please read the "why it is not visible yet" section before closing.

Raised during review of #50918 by @nikJ13, confirmed by @suryansh29, and split
out here on his suggestion so the fix in #50918 can stay narrow.

#### The interaction

`Step3p5ReasoningParser` post-processes the base class's return value
(`vllm/reasoning/step3p5_reasoning_parser.py`, lines 95-105 on `main`):

```python
def extract_reasoning(self, model_output, request):
    reasoning, content = super().extract_reasoning(model_output, request)
    if reasoning is not None:
        reasoning = reasoning.removesuffix("\n")
    if content is not None:
        content = content.removeprefix("\n")
    return reasoning or None, content or None
```

The intent is documented a few lines below, in the streaming path: *"Drop the
immediate newline that models often emit after `</think>`."* So the strip targets
the beginning of the text that follows the end token.

Today the base class returns exactly that, and the strip lands correctly.

After #50918 the base returns `content_before + content_after`, where
`content_before` is text the model produced *before* the start token. When that
prefix is non-empty, two things go wrong at once:

- the newline the strip was meant to remove is no longer at index 0, so it survives
- the newline now at index 0 belongs to `content_before` and is removed instead

#### Worked example

For `model_output = "\nIntro<think>reasoning</think>\nAnswer"`:

```text
content_before = '\nIntro'
content_after  = '\nAnswer'

intended                    -> '\nIntroAnswer'
main today                  -> 'Answer'          (correct; no prefix exists to lose)
after #50918, then Step3p5  -> 'Intro\nAnswer'   both errors visible
```

#### Why it is not visible yet

On `main` the base discards `content_before` entirely — that discard is the bug
#50918 fixes. With the prefix gone, `content` always starts with the newline that
follows `</think>`, so `removeprefix("\n")` does the right thing by accident. The
misalignment only appears once the prefix is preserved, which is why no existing
test covers it.

`step3p5` is the only subclass of `BaseThi

issues.title: [Bug]: Mistral-Small-3.1 FP8 (Pixtral) returns NaN on image inputs with compilation enabled; works with --enforce-eager
issues.body_head:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment</summary>

- vLLM: v0.24.0
- Hardware: 1x NVIDIA H100 80GB (tensor-parallel-size 1)
- Model: `RedHatAI/Mistral-Small-3.1-24B-Instruct-2503-FP8-dynamic` (compressed-tensors FP8-dynamic; only the language-model `Linear` layers are quantized — `vision_tower`, `multi_modal_projector`, and `lm_head` are in the `ignore` list and stay bf16)
- Served as `PixtralForConditionalGeneration` (via `--config-format mistral`)

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With this FP8 Mistral-Small-3.1 (Pixtral) checkpoint, **text/chat/tool/structured requests work fine, but any request that includes an image returns `NaN`**. The engine does not crash; the API fails to serialize the response:

```
openai.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'Out of range float values are not JSON compliant: nan', ...}}
```

Server-side, the request completes (HTTP 200 path) but the generated logits/logprobs contain `NaN`, so `json.dumps` in `create_chat_completion` raises `ValueError: Out of range float values are not JSON compliant: nan`.

**Key finding: the NaN only occurs with compilation enabled. Adding `--enforce-eager` makes image requests produce valid output.** So this appears to be a torch.compile / cudagraph issue on the FP8 multimodal path rather than pure FP8 numerical instability (the quantized decoder is fine for text; it only goes NaN once image embeddings are in the sequence, and only when compiled).

Text-only requests are unaffected in both modes.

#### Reproduce

Fails (image → NaN):
```bash
vllm serve RedHatAI/Mistral-Small-3.1-24B-Instruct-2503-FP8-dynamic \
  --tokenizer-mode mistral --config-format mistral --max-model-len 32768
# then send any chat request containing an image_url -> response contains NaN -> 400
```

issues.title: [Bug]: speculative decoding under pipeline parallelism produces wrong output with --no-async-scheduling
issues.body_head:
### Your current environment

vLLM `0.26.1rc1.dev693+g7f7a32cfe` (nightly), 8× RTX 3090 (sm_86), CUDA 12.x,
`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`. Reproduced at `pipeline_parallel_size` 2, 4 and 8,
with two different speculative methods and two model families. Code references
are against `main` @ `98f86b9c0232`.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `--no-async-scheduling`, speculative decoding under pipeline parallelism
produces wrong output — or a CUDA fault — instead of being rejected or working.
Turning async scheduling back on fixes it.

### Root cause

`next_decode_eligible_step` is assigned in exactly one place in the tree:

```
vllm/v1/core/sched/async_scheduler.py:49
    request.next_decode_eligible_step = self.current_step + self.pp_size
```

initialised in one place:

```
vllm/v1/request.py:167
    self.next_decode_eligible_step = 0
```

and read in exactly one place:

```
vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:509
    if self.current_step < request.next_decode_eligible_step:
        # V2+PP+async: enforce `pp_size` steps between same-req decodes
        # to match worker-side sampled-tokens broadcast slot ring cadence.
```

The base `Scheduler` — which is what `--no-async-scheduling` selects — reads that
field and never sets it. It stays `0`, the guard never fires, and nothing keeps a
request's decodes `pp_size` steps apart. The worker-side sampled-token broadcast
ring is then read out of phase.

### What that produces, measured

A probe at the point where a step's input ids are built
(`combine_sampled_and_draft_tokens`), PP=2:

```
last_sampled=[16925]  drafts=[16925, 16925, 16925]    healthy
last_sampled=[0]      drafts=[0, 0, 0]                ~25% of spec steps
```

Token id 0 is embedded as the anchor. On the model under test token 0 is `!`, and
the generated text fills with `!`. The same skew has a second face — the step gets
scheduled without the accepted token that its drafts hang off:

```
healthy:  hidden=(4,1024)  logits_indices=[0, 1, 2, 3]   qlen=4  num_logits=4  ndraft=3
failing:  hidden=(3,1024)  logits_indices=[-1, 0, 1, 2]  qlen=3  num_logits=4  ndraft=3
```

`logits_start = query_end - num_logits = 3 - 4 = -1`, so
`hidden_states[input_batch.logits_indices]` either wraps to the last row silently
(torch semantics) or trips:

```
Assertion `ind >=0 && ind < ind_dim_size && "vectorized gather kernel index out of bounds"` failed
```

`v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py`, wh

Base image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.0-cu129-ubuntu2404

After a failed NIXL/HMA receive, DeepSeek-V4 can return HTTP 200 with corrupted
tokens in `reasoning` and an empty `content` field. Clients that read only
`choices[].message.content` see an apparently empty response. Disabling
thinking exposes the corrupted output in `content` instead.

--speculative-config \

--kv-transfer-config \
'{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail"}'
```

Send chat-completion requests with `max_tokens=128` using:

1. the default request;
2. thinking explicitly enabled;
3. thinking explicitly disabled; and

asymmetric configuration fails the NIXL compatibility handshake. No KV transfer
completes successfully, but the requests resume decoding.

issues.title: [Bug]: Alignment specialization on causal_conv1d metadata pointers forces inference-time JIT compiles; raced shared-cache writes produced silent all-NaN outputs
issues.body_head:
### Summary

`_causal_conv1d_fwd_kernel` and `_causal_conv1d_update_kernel` let Triton specialize on the 16-byte alignment of their metadata pointers (`cache_indices_ptr`, `query_start_loc_ptr`, `conv_state_indices_ptr`, ...).

Three facts make this a problem:

1. **The specialization buys nothing here.** These arrays are read one scalar at a time (a block index, an offset), so the aligned and unaligned binaries run at the same speed. Alignment specialization only pays off for wide vectorized loads (`x_ptr`, `w_ptr`, ... — not these args).
2. **Their alignment flips at runtime.** They are per-step slices of batch metadata, so the address offset depends on the batch layout of that step.
3. **Warmup can never cover the unaligned variant.** Warmup tensors are freshly allocated and therefore always aligned. So the first compile of the unaligned variant is guaranteed to happen *during inference* — this is (part of) the latency spike tracked in #43009, and `jit_monitor` (#45631) duly warns about it.

In a multi-node deployment this goes from a latency nuisance to a correctness bug.

### What we hit

GRPO RL training, Nemotron-3-Super-120B, 6 vLLM engines on 6 GB200 nodes, with a shared `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` on Lustre (for warm starts). Engines intermittently returned **all-NaN logits from the first prefill token** — only for long prompts, only on some engines, and unreproducible afterwards.

Disk forensics (no repro needed):

- These kernels compiled to disk exactly 3 times; the mtimes match the 3 NaN windows one-to-one. After the cache filled up: 40+ clean rounds, zero recurrence.
- Two cache hash dirs for the same kernel appeared **within the same minute**, differing only in the `tt.divisibility=16` attribute on `cache_indices_ptr` — two nodes concurrently compiling the aligned/unaligned variants into the same shared dir. Triton's cache group write (`__grp__*.json` + cubin) is not atomic across writers.
- Every failing request was ≥143K tokens (its `cache_indices` slice lands at an unaligned offset); every success ≤138K. Only some engines were poisoned — the race losers.

A race loser ends up running the aligned-assumption binary on unaligned `cache_indices` → reads wrong block indices → garbage → all-NaN logits, silently.

Sharing `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` across nodes is on us, and we now scope it per node. But the variant axis itself has no upside, and single-node users still pay the inference-time compile spike for it.

issues.title: [Bug]: Triton MoE and block-FP8 GEMMs mishandle the K tile — an out-of-bounds weight read, and wrong scales when a tile spans two quantization groups
issues.body_head:
## Summary

Two Triton GEMMs used by quantized MoE serving get the K tile wrong, and in both cases a sibling code path already does it correctly.

1. **`fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq` reads the packed weights out of bounds.** The kernel builds `k_mask` whenever `K` is not a multiple of `BLOCK_SIZE_K` and applies it to the scale load and to *both* zero-point loads, but the weight load itself is unmasked, so the last K iteration reads past the end of the weight tensor. The sibling `fused_moe_kernel` masks the identical load. The numbers that come back are multiplied by a scale that *is* masked to zero, so the arithmetic result is unaffected — this is a memory-safety bug, not a numerical one.

2. **`w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm` can pick one scale for a tile that spans several quantization groups.** `_w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm` reads a single scale pair per K tile, indexed by `(k * BLOCK_SIZE_K) // group_k`, which is correct only when `BLOCK_SIZE_K` divides `group_k`. Nothing enforces it, and the comment above the default config states the requirement inverted — "BLOCK_SIZE_K must be divisible by block_size[1]" — which is exactly the configuration that breaks. The fused-MoE launcher clamps this (`BLOCK_SIZE_K = min(BLOCK_SIZE_K, min(block_shape[0], block_shape[1]))`); this one does not.

Neither is caught today because the shipped defaults stay inside the safe range: `w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm`'s default config sets `BLOCK_SIZE_K = block_k`, and `test_fused_moe_wn16` only uses `k` values of 128 and 1024, which are multiples of every `BLOCK_SIZE_K` the untuned path picks. The exposure in both cases is the tuning-config lookup, which reads `BLOCK_SIZE_K` straight out of a JSON file in `configs/` — and the wna16 files there already carry `BLOCK_SIZE_K` values of 128 (168 entries) and 256 (118 entries).

The GPTQ/AWQ MoE kernel was added in #12185 and the block-FP8 GEMM in #11523.

## Reproduction

Both scripts drive the library's own launchers — `dispatch_fused_moe_kernel` and `w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm` compute the grid and every kernel argument — against this repo at HEAD, installed with `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 pip install -e .`.

**1. Out-of-bounds weight read.** An int4 `w4a16` MoE matmul through `invoke_fused_moe_kernel`, with `K = 96` and `BLOCK_SIZE_K = 64`. The packed weight tensor is `[E, N, K // 2]` uint8, so each row holds 48 bytes while the loop covers 64. The weight tensor is allocated last so that the overrun lands in unallocated memory rather tha

issues.title: [Bug]: two logger calls have mismatched %-args, so the log record is dropped
issues.body_head:
Two `logger` calls pass arguments that don't match their format string. When either one fires, the logging module raises internally and the message you wanted is replaced by a `--- Logging error ---` traceback on stderr.

The first is in `vllm/v1/engine/tensor_ipc.py` at lines 151 to 153:

```python
logger.warning(
    "Discarding %d stale tensors from sender %s",
    sender_id,
)
```

Two placeholders and one argument, so this raises `TypeError: not enough arguments for format string`. There's a second problem in the same call: `sender_id` is annotated `str` at line 135, so it can't fill the `%d` slot regardless of ordering, and putting it first instead gives `TypeError: %d format: a number is required, not str`. The count that `%d` is asking for looks like it should come from the dict popped just above it, given that `_Sender.tensors` is `dict[int, dict[int, torch.Tensor]]` at line 111.

The second is in `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/moriio/moriio_connector.py` at lines 1501 to 1504:

```python
logger.debug(
    "MoRIIO handshake listener received done recv for req",
    req_id.decode(),
)
```

No placeholder at all and one argument, which gives `TypeError: not all arguments converted during string formatting`, so the request id never makes it into the log. This one is debug level so it matters less, but it's the same mistake.

I reproduced both of these with plain `logging` on a stock interpreter to confirm the record really is dropped rather than just formatted oddly.

There was a third instance of this in `quick_all_reduce.py`, but #39127 is already open for it so I've left it alone.
