issues.title: [Bug]: `find_mm_placeholders` may return an incorrect position for `PromptInsertion`
issues.body_head:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Description

When `PromptInsertion` inserts tokens that overlap with adjacent tokens in the original prompt, `find_mm_placeholders` may locate an earlier occurrence instead of the tokens inserted by the prompt update.

For example:

- Original prompt contains `[32000]` at index 3.
- The insertion target is `[32000]`.
- The inserted placeholder tokens are `[32000, 32000]`.

After applying the update, the resulting sequence around the target is:

```text
[..., 32000, 32000, 32000, ...]
      original  inserted
```

The inserted placeholder starts at index 4. However, `find_mm_placeholders` scans the resulting prompt for `[32000, 32000]` and finds the sequence starting at index 3, which includes one token from the original prompt.

## Expected behavior

The placeholder position should refer to the tokens inserted by `PromptInsertion`, so `start_idx` should be 4.

## Actual behavior

`find_mm_placeholders` reports `start_idx=3`.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

issues.title: [Bug][Spec Decode] All-NaN logits row is laundered into an out-of-vocab token id by the rejection sampler (device assert far from origin); NaN-metric blind spot on the verify path; uninit-scratch audit
issues.body_head:
## TL;DR

If any verification row of `target_logits` is all-NaN (numerics upset in the model forward — whatever the cause), the V2 GPU-worker rejection sampler does not fail or fall back: its NaN-poisoned block-argmax chain **emits a token id equal to `vocab_size` exactly**, which propagates through `last_sampled_tokens` → `combine_sampled_and_draft_tokens` → `input_ids` and detonates 1–3 steps later as:

```
/pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Indexing.cu:1524: indexSelectSmallIndex:
Assertion `srcIndex < srcSelectDimSize` failed.
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered
```

surfacing asynchronously (typically in `AsyncOutput.get_output → copy_event.synchronize()`), far from the origin. We reproduced and instrumented this end-to-end ~10 times. Open issue #42261 (gemma4 + MTP, same assert, intermittent, restart clears it) matches this signature and is plausibly the same bug.

Independently, the engine's only NaN detector cannot see these rows (§ NaN-metric gap), and the same file contains a family of latent uninitialized-scratch hazards (§ audit).

## Mechanism (fully instrumented)

Configuration: spec decode (dspark; greedy drafts → one-hot verification path), FULL decode cudagraphs, TP4, sustained mixed traffic. All findings verified against `main` as of 2026-08-17.

1. A verification row of `target_logits` arrives **all-NaN** (in our case the numerics fault was in a custom SM80 attention kernel amplifying garbage KV reads — not upstream's code — but any NaN row triggers the rest).
2. In the verify kernel, acceptance comparisons against NaN are false → the position is rejected.
3. `_rejection_resample_kernel` computes the one-hot residual of the NaN row (still NaN), adds gumbel noise (still NaN), and stores per-block maxima/argmaxes. Captured block dump from a live event, `RESAMPLE_BLOCK_SIZE=1024`, vocab 129280 → 127 blocks:

   local_max[0..125] = NaN            (argmax = each block's last lane — NaN-poisoned tl.max)
   local_max[126]    = -inf           (its 768 masked padding lanes beat NaN in this comparator order)
   local_argmax[126] = 129280         (= 126*1024 + 256, the first PADDED lane)
   ```
4. `_insert_resampled_kernel`'s cross-block `tl.argmax` over `[NaN ×126, -inf]` is NaN-poisoned and selects block 126, loads `local_argmax[126] = 129280 = vocab_size`, and **stores it into a valid slot of `sampled`**.
5. `post_update` copies it to `last_sampled_tokens`; the next step's `combine_sampled_and_draft_tokens` wr

issues.title: [Bug]: Prefill misdispatched into spec-decode FULL cudagraph when prompt length == 1 + num_speculative_tokens → silent GDN state loss, garbage output (hybrid/Qwen3-Next models)
issues.body_head:
## Summary

When speculative decoding is enabled, a **prefill** whose scheduled token count happens to equal `uniform_decode_query_len * num_reqs` is misclassified as a uniform-decode batch and dispatched into the **FULL cudagraph captured for spec-decode**. For hybrid models with GDN/linear-attention layers (e.g. Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5-MoE), this silently skips **all recurrent-state writes** for that request: every subsequent decode step then computes from a zero initial state, producing deterministic garbage output and a collapsed draft acceptance rate.

The trigger is absurdly easy to hit: with `num_speculative_tokens=2`, **any 3-token prompt** (e.g. the Chinese prompt `中国的首都是` under the Qwen tokenizer) poisons the request from its very first step.

I have root-caused this with per-block checksums of the GDN state pools and verified a one-line-of-logic fix. Code on current `main` is identical to what I debugged on 0.27.1.

## Root cause

`GPUModelRunner._is_uniform_decode` (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py) is a **pure shape check**:

```python
return (
    ((max_num_scheduled_tokens == uniform_decode_query_len)
     and (num_tokens == max_num_scheduled_tokens * num_reqs))
    if force_uniform_decode is None
    else force_uniform_decode
)
```

With MTP `k=2`, `uniform_decode_query_len = 1 + 2 = 3`. A virgin single request whose prompt is exactly 3 tokens gives `max_num_scheduled_tokens == 3` and `num_tokens == 3 * 1`, so the **prefill** is classified as uniform decode and `cudagraph_dispatcher.dispatch(..., uniform_decode=True)` routes it into the FULL graph captured for spec-decode.

The failure mechanism for GDN layers:

1. The GDN metadata builder correctly classifies the step as a prefill (`num_prefills=1, num_spec_decodes=0`), **but** the persistent-buffer refresh in `GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build()` only happens in the spec/decode branches (gated on `num_prefills == 0`). A prefill build never touches the persistent buffers.
2. The FULL graph replays with **stale capture-time metadata**: `spec_state_indices_tensor` still holds `0 == NULL_BLOCK_ID` from `build_for_cudagraph_capture`.
3. The FLA kernels (`fused_recurrent`, `fused_sigmoid_gating`) and `causal_conv1d_update` all have null-block guards that **silently skip stores** when the state index is `NULL_BLOCK_ID` — correct padding hygiene, but here it swallows the entire prefill state write.
4. The request's conv/SSM states stay zero forever. The first sampled token already diverges; everyt

Observed on main @ eac636a7fa476983cdae34b45a984e9852aad375 (NVIDIA H200, driver 580.159.03, CUDA 13.0).

`tests/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py::test_reshape_and_cache_per_token_head` fails in the int4 branch (`kv_quant_mode=INT4_PER_TOKEN_HEAD`, `quant_min=-8.0`, `quant_max=7.0`): the dequantized round-trip (unpack nibbles → zero-point → scale → inverse RHT) lands far outside the assertion tolerance (atol=rtol=0.5) vs the bf16 reference.

**Deterministic failure** — head_size=64, num_kv_heads=1, num_tokens=42 (seed 0, block_size 16), i.e. `[int4-0-16-64-1-42]`. Fails on every run with identical mismatch statistics (inputs are seed-deterministic):

```
AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!
Mismatched elements: 35 / 64 (54.7%)
Greatest absolute difference: 3.0546875 at index (0, 38) (up to 0.5 allowed)
Greatest relative difference: 3651.2666015625 at index (0, 52) (up to 0.5 allowed)
```

**Flaky failures** — pass/fail flips across runs on identical code:

- head_size=128, num_kv_heads=1, num_tokens=42 (`[int4-0-16-128-1-42]`): 64/128 (50.0%) mismatched, abs 4.002 @ (0, 70), rel 25.5 @ (0, 101)
- head_size=64, num_kv_heads=4, num_tokens=7 (`[int4-0-16-64-4-7]`): 149/256 (58.2%) mismatched, abs 3.93 @ (2, 26), rel 256 @ (0, 37)

All int8 and fp8 parametrizations, and the remaining int4 combos, pass consistently.

**Minimal repro:**

```bash
pytest tests/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py \
  -k "test_reshape_and_cache_per_token_head and int4-0-16-64-1-42"
```

**Analysis:** the kernel under test is `vllm.v1.attention.ops.triton_reshape_and_cache_flash.triton_reshape_and_cache_flash_per_token_head_quant` (assertion at `tests/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py:256`). A deterministic 54.7% element mismatch at ~6x the allowed absolute tolerance rules out tolerance noise and points to a correctness defect in the int4 pack/RHT path (candidate causes: zero-point packing or nibble ordering). The two shape-dependent flaky combos additionally suggest a race or uninitialized/leftover cache state whose manifestation depends on shape/head layout.

The qcfg fixture carries IDs int4/int8/fp8; the stacked parametrize resolves bottom-up, so `[int4-0-16-64-1-42]` = seed 0, block_size 16, head_size 64, num_kv_heads 1, num_tokens 42. All failing combos share seed 0 / block_size 16, but those are the only values in `SEEDS`/`BLOCK_SIZES`, so there is no signal there.

Happy to collect a failing-tensor dump if that helps isolate it.

issues.title: [Bug]: bare assert in BasevLLMParameter._assert_and_load gives no diagnostics on weight shape mismatch
issues.body_head:
### Your current environment

0.27.1 
env - doesn't matter for this

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Loading a checkpoint whose scale tensor has the wrong shape fails with a bare AssertionError — no parameter name, no shapes, no hint what to fix.

  File "vllm/model_executor/parameter.py", line 94, in _assert_and_load
      assert self.data.shape == loaded_weight.shape or self._is_1d_and_scalar(
  AssertionError

Repro: compressed-tensors FP8, strategy: channel, weight_scale written as [out] instead of [out, 1]. The checkpoint is at fault, but the error says nothing about which parameter or which shapes collide. It took a debugger to find; the message below  would have made it a one-line fix.

vLLM reports the analogous case well elsewhere — a missing parameter raises ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'fc.weight_scale' in ... and lists the available names.

Second concern: assert is stripped under python -O. self.data.copy_(loaded_weight) then runs unchecked, and copy_ broadcasts — a 1-element per-tensor scale would be silently spread across all channels instead of rejected.

Patch (no signature change; the parameter does not carry its name, so shapes only):

```
     def _assert_and_load(self, loaded_weight: torch.Tensor):
-        assert self.data.shape == loaded_weight.shape or self._is_1d_and_scalar(
-            loaded_weight
-        )
+        if self.data.shape != loaded_weight.shape and not self._is_1d_and_scalar(
+            loaded_weight
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"weight shape mismatch: parameter has {tuple(self.data.shape)}, "
+                f"checkpoint has {tuple(loaded_weight.shape)}"
+            )
         self.data.copy_(loaded_weight)
```

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

issues.title: [Bug] Hybrid mamba align precopy: illegal memory access on prefix-cache resume with explicit --block-size (state column seeded with wrong block size)
issues.body_head:
### Your current environment

vLLM 0.27.1, V2 GPU runner, single RTX 3090 (SM86), CUDA 12.x, WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 (also reproduces the same way on bare metal by code inspection). Model: Qwen3.8-27B (hybrid GDN/mamba + full attention), W4A16.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`MambaHybridModelState.add_request` (v1/worker/gpu/model_states/mamba_hybrid.py) seeds the running mamba state column with the **CLI/attention block size** instead of the **mamba KV-cache group's block size**:

```python
self._mamba_state_idx_gpu[req_index].fill_(
    (new_req_data.num_computed_tokens - 1) // self.cache_config.block_size
)
```

On hybrid models the mamba group's `block_size` is derived from page matching (e.g. 2176 for a Qwen3-Next-style hybrid) and generally differs from `cache_config.block_size` whenever the user passes `--block-size` explicitly (required e.g. for quantized-KV setups whose tile size dictates the block, in our case 128).

With `--block-size 128 --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align`, the **second** request over a cached prefix crashes: a resume with `num_computed_tokens=100096` seeds `state_idx = (100096-1)//128 = 781` instead of `(100096-1)//2176 = 45`. The fused align precopy (`precopy_mamba_align_fused_kernel`) then reads `block_table[req, 781]` in a table with only ~61 columns, gets a garbage block id, and dies with:

```
RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access was encountered
  File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/mamba_hybrid.py", line 201, in preprocess_state
  File "vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py", line 826, in run_fused_precopy
```

(confirmed as the faulting kernel with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`).

First requests are unaffected (`num_computed == 0` seeds `-1` regardless of divisor), so in practice this looks like a spurious crash that only appears on the second request over a >1-block cached prefix — easy to misattribute.

**Repro:** any hybrid (mamba+attention) model with `--block-size <n>` where n != the mamba group block size, `--enable-prefix-caching`, `--mamba-cache-mode align`; send the same multi-block prompt twice.

### Fix (verified)

Seed with the mamba spec's block size. `_mamba_spec` is populated lazily by the first batch's `preprocess_state`; a resume can only happen after some batch has run, and fresh requests seed `-1` either way, so the fallback is safe:

```python
mamba_bs = (self._mamba_spec.block_size
            if self._mamba_spec is not None
            else self.cache_config.block_size)
self._mamba_st

Image `vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:nightly` (image id c48edf76bb9f): vLLM 0.26.1rc1.dev942+g5a4c8d992, torch 2.13.0+xpu, auto-round-lib 0.14.2. Single Intel Arc Pro B70 (BMG-G31, 32 GB), host kernel 7.1.0-070100, NEO 26.27.39122.11, IGC 2.38.2. Full `collect_env` on request.

We checked that the corruption is identical on both. We did not re-check the throughput numbers on the stock wheel, so treat those as measured against 0.1.14.dev11 rather than against the image as published.

Model: Intel/Qwen3.6-27B-int4-AutoRound, `quantization_config: {bits: 4, group_size: 128, sym: true, quant_method: auto-round, packing_format: auto_round:auto_gptq}`. A 9B AutoRound int4 checkpoint (Intel/Qwen3.5-9B-int4-AutoRound, same recipe) showed partial corruption in the same configuration, 2/60 accepted, which is a milder presentation than the 27B's.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Serving an AutoRound int4 checkpoint with default settings, a single request at a time is correct. Send two or more at once and every response becomes garbage:

```
'The quick pon死不IKEOfTypeaceyüp风险防范-commentsoshibigint...'
'The_META_suite仑rap扎扎实ocos浩गत дер优ippers.gradient金花anyi...'
'The_META_suite仑rap扎扎实ocos浩गत дер优ippers.gradient金花anyi...'
```

Three concurrent copies of one temperature-0 prompt, no speculative decoding, nothing unusual in the config. There is no error, no warning, and no log line. The same thing happens on every speculative decoding verify step, which is how we originally found it, but concurrency is the trigger that matters: on this hardware and with cudagraph capture enabled, any deployment serving more than one user at a time is silently producing this. Capture is opt-in on XPU (`VLLM_XPU_ENABLE_XPU_GRAPH=1`; `platforms/xpu.py:300` otherwise forces `cudagraph_mode` to NONE), so this is not the out-of-the-box default. The condition is decode steps carrying more than one token per forward. Single-request non-speculative decode is one token per forward, which is the only safe shape and the reason this survives casual testing.

Underneath, quantized linears are returning **zeros**. Not drift, not wrong values. We captured `ark.woqgemm` in a `torch.xpu` graph outside vLLM entirely, with synthetic weights and no checkpoint: at m = 1 replay is bit-exact

issues.title: [Bug]: FP8 KV cache causes systematic decode/prefill logprob mismatch on Hopper FA3
issues.body_head:
## Your current environment

```text
OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64), kernel 5.15.0-119-generic
Python: 3.11.15
vLLM: 0.28.0 (also reproduced on 0.27.1)
PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130
CUDA runtime: 13.0
NVIDIA driver: 580.159.03
GPU: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3
Model: Qwen3-4B (BF16 weights)
Attention backend: FLASH_ATTN (FlashAttention 3)
KV cache dtype: fp8 / fp8_e4m3; control: auto (BF16)
Prefix caching: disabled
Execution mode: eager
End-to-end comparison: VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 (set before importing vLLM)
```

## 🐛 Describe the bug

### Summary

With FP8 KV cache, vLLM returns systematically different logprobs depending on whether a token is scored through decode (token-by-token generation) or through a full-prefill rescore (`prompt_logprobs` on the same sequence). On Qwen3-4B (H100, vLLM 0.28.0, greedy, 224 generated tokens, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`), the first mismatch is at absolute sequence position **97**, with 115–117 mismatching generated-token positions and max `|Δlogprob|` ≈ 0.56. The root cause is in the bundled FlashAttention 3 Hopper FP8 kernel (`vllm-project/flash-attention`): decode and prefill select different KV tile widths (`kBlockN=96` vs `192` at `head_dim=128`), and a direct FA3 kernel reproducer below shows the same boundary at KV length `seqlen_k=97`.

### End-to-end reproduction

1. Greedy-generate 224 tokens with `logprobs=1`; record each output token's logprob.
2. Concatenate prompt + output; run a full-prefill rescore with `prompt_logprobs`.
3. Compare logprob at each generated-token position.

Set `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` before importing vLLM.

**Observed (unpatched, vLLM 0.28.0, FP8 KV cache):**

| Prompt | First mismatch position | Mismatching positions | Max `\|Δlogprob\|` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `tell me a story` | 97 | 115 / 224 | 0.50 |
| `讲个故事` | 97 | 117 / 224 | 0.40 |

Without `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, decode and one-shot prefill can differ even with BF16 because of unrelated batch-shape effects. Those differences must not be used alone to attribute a residual to this FA3 FP8 kernel bug.

### Minimal kernel reproduction

The test calls `vllm.vllm_flash_attn.flash_attn_varlen_func` twice with the same FP8 K/V tensors and the same final query row: once as a full causal query (prefill), and once as a one-row query (decode).

```python

from vllm.vllm_flash_attn import flash_attn_varlen_func

device = "cuda"
nheads_q, nheads_kv, head_dim = 12, 2, 128

def run(seqlen):
    torch.manual_seed(42)
    k = torch.randn

### Your current environment

NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor (Blackwell, **sm_110**), JetPack 7 / L4T R38.2.0, CUDA 13.0, aarch64.
vLLM built from source at `main` (`6a9c69fa`) with `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=11.0f`.
Model: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (`Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, hybrid Gated-DeltaNet + full attention, MTP speculative decoding).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Two related issues prevent the fused GDN decode kernel from ever being used on sm_110 (Jetson Thor).

#### 1. `FUSED_GDN_DECODE_ARCHS` omits `11.0f`

`CMakeLists.txt` (line ~1122):

```cmake
cuda_archs_loose_intersection(FUSED_GDN_DECODE_ARCHS
  "8.0;8.6;8.9;9.0a;10.0f;12.0f" "${CUDA_ARCHS}")
```

Both `10.0f` (datacenter Blackwell) and `12.0f` (consumer Blackwell) are present, but `11.0f` (Thor) is not. Neighbouring lists in the same CUDA-13 block do include it — e.g. `SCALED_MM_ARCHS "10.0f;10.7f;11.0f"` and `FP4_SM100_ARCHS "10.0f;10.7f;11.0f"` — which suggests an oversight rather than intent.

Consequence at runtime on Thor:

```
INFO [qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py] Falling back to the Triton GDN decode path:
     torch.ops._C.fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp is not built
INFO [qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py] GDN decode kernel: triton
```

For Qwen3.5/3.8-class hybrid models this affects 48 of 64 layers on the MTP decode path.

#### 2. Declaration guard mismatch in `csrc/libtorch_stable/ops.h` (not Thor-specific)

Adding `11.0f` to the list above then fails to compile:

```
csrc/libtorch_stable/torch_bindings.cpp:804:23: error:
  'fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp' was not declared in this scope
     TORCH_BOX(&fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp));
```

Cause: in `ops.h` the declaration of `fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp` (line ~396) sits **inside** the `#ifdef VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_KDA_DECODE` block opened at line 384 and closed at line 407 — while `torch_bindings.cpp` gates both the `ops.def` (line ~532) and the `ops.impl` (line ~803) on `#ifdef VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_GDN_DECODE`.

This is normally invisible because `FUSED_KDA_DECODE_ARCHS` (`9.0a;10.0f;12.0f`) is a subset of `FUSED_GDN_DECODE_ARCHS`, so both macros are always defined together. **It is not Thor-specific** — any build whose `CUDA_ARCHS` intersects GDN but not KDA (e.g. `8.0`, `8.6`, `8.9` alone) hits the same error.

### Fix

Both changes are one-liners; happy to open a PR.

```diff
--- a/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/CMakeLists.txt
     cuda_archs_loose_intersection(FUSED_GDN_DECODE_ARCHS
-      "8.0;8.6;8.9;9.0a;10.0f;12.0f" "${CUDA_ARCHS}")
+      "8.0;8.6;8.9;

issues.title: [Bug]: RETRACTED — duplicate of #53142 (my "equal block sizes" premise was wrong; see closing comment)
issues.body_head:
### Your current environment

- Hardware: NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, `sm_121`, aarch64, 121 GiB unified memory), single GPU, TP=1
- vLLM: `v0.1.dev20073+g8e685d198` — the NVIDIA preview build for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (image `vllm/vllm-openai:qwen38-flash-next-arm64-cu130`), V2 GPU model runner (`Using V2 Model Runner` in boot log)
- Model: `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` (176B hybrid: GDN linear attention + QSA sparse attention + full attention), `--max-model-len 262144`, `--max-num-seqs 8`
- Flags: `--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align`; **no explicit `--block-size`** — the engine derives it itself and prints `Setting attention block size to 1600 tokens to ensure that attention page size is >= mamba page size` (with MTP k=2) / `800 tokens` + `Padding mamba page size by 0.25% ... exactly equal` (without spec). So attention and mamba block sizes are **equal** in every run below.

Build vs current main, checked file-by-file inside the image: `v1/attention/backends/gdn_attn.py` is within ~25 minor lines of main; the scheduler has `_mamba_block_aligned_split`; `v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py` has `drop_eagle_block`; `v1/kv_cache_interface.py` has **no** `supports_eagle_cache_peek` (the last piece of #47861). I know a dev build is not pristine main — reporting anyway because the crash site is upstream code (`run_fused_precopy` / `precopy_mamba_align_fused_kernel` exist on main today) and #53142, the only open report against this kernel, just lost its live reproduction. This one is deterministic.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

CUDA illegal memory access in `precopy_mamba_align_fused_kernel` when a request is **admitted with a prefix-cache hit while the request that produced those cached blocks is still in flight (or finishes in the same scheduler step)**. Distinct from #53142: block sizes are equal here, so the `add_request` seed divisor is identical either way and the one-line fix proposed there cannot be the whole story.

Measured matrix (46,005-token shared prefix, 6 boots, 100% reproducible):

| scenario | result |
|---|---|
| cold 46k prompt, b=1 | ✅ OK |
| **same 46k prompt again, strictly sequential** (donor finished long before; `hits=43200` = 27×1600) | ✅ OK, 8.9× faster — resume path genuinely taken |
| **two concurrent requests sharing the 46k prefix** | 🔴 dies in 1.2–23 s, every boot |
| same, with `--max-num-seqs 1` | 🔴 still dies — see dump below |
| same, with `--no-async-scheduling` (different step path, `core.py step()`) | 🔴 still dies |

issues.title: compressed-tensors config collapses GDN linear-attention token distinctness (qwen4exp/hybrid MoE models produce garbage; identical weights clean under fp8 config)
issues.body_head:
## Bug: compressed-tensors quantization config collapses GDN (gated-delta-net) linear attention token distinctness — Qwen4Exp/qwen3.8-class hybrid models produce garbage under ANY CT config, identical weights run clean under fp8 config

### Environment
- vLLM: `0.28.0+strix` (kyuz0 TheRock gfx1151 build, but the implicated code paths — compressed-tensors model wrap + GDN/FLA attention — are architecture-generic)
- Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration`), 48 decoder layers, hybrid GDN linear attention + QSA full attention + MoE (512 experts) + PLE n-gram embedding
- Hardware: AMD Radeon 8060S (gfx1151), ROCm; reproduced single-GPU TP=1 (should be HW-independent since the failure is representational, not numerical-precision)

### Summary

Converting an fp8 checkpoint to a compressed-tensors W4A16 checkpoint (int4-g64/g32 symmetric, group scales, standard `weight_packed`/`weight_scale` layout — byte-verified against llmcompressor reference models) makes generation collapse to repetition soup. **The same model files, loader, and code produce correct output when served with the original fp8 quantization_config.** Through a nine-stage elimination (details below), every quantization-related component was proven byte- and math-exact; the failure is that **GDN linear-attention layers collapse hidden-state token distinctness whenever a compressed-tensors config is present on the model — even when the CT group targets only `RoutedExperts` and every GDN Linear resolves to `UnquantizedLinearMethod`.**

### Reproduction

1. Serve a hybrid GDN+MoE checkpoint with any `quantization_config: {"quant_method": "compressed-tensors", ...}` (group targeting only routed experts; GDN/attention/embeddings all in `ignore`).
2. Send any chat completion. Output is multilingual repetition soup.
3. Re-serve the identical weights with the original fp8 quantization_config → correct output.
4. Zero out routed experts entirely (monkeypatch `TritonWNA16Experts.apply` to write zeros) under the CT config → output becomes clean EOS (no soup), **but hidden states still collapse**, proving the routed-expert path is not the cause.

### Key evidence (hidden-state sweep)

Per-layer self-cosine of decoder-layer input hidden states (78-token real prefill):

| config | L0 entry | L1 entry | L2 entry | L47 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fp8 config (works) | 0.05 | ~0.05–0.1 | healthy | healthy |
| CT config (soup) | 0.05 | 0.40 | 0.55, norm 5.5e8 | 0.43, norm 2.3e10 |
| CT config + exp

issues.title: [Bug]: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next generates corrupted Thai orthography under vLLM; the same model under llama.cpp at the same QSA budget is clean
issues.body_head:
### Summary

`Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` under vLLM produces systematically malformed Thai: single-character substitutions, displaced tone marks and doubled combining marks. The same model at the same effective QSA budget under llama.cpp is clean — 0 defects across 130 samples versus 12–18 per 1000 Thai characters across five vLLM configurations.

This was originally reported as part of #54521 (non-determinism from `persistent_topk`). It is a **separate defect**: I have since shown non-determinism is not its cause, and that QSA block selection is not either. Splitting it out so #54521 can stay scoped to determinism.

### Environment

- 2x DGX Spark GB10 (sm_121), `-tp 2`, aarch64, driver 580.159.03 / 580.95.05
- vLLM `0.1.dev20073+g8e685d198` (official `vllm/vllm-openai:qwen38-flash-next` body)
- `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`, `--enforce-eager`, stock `indexer_budget=2048`
- Sampling: the model card's temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 20. **Greedy is not usable for a quality measurement on this model** — it degenerates even at 105 prompt tokens — so every number below is a rate over 10 samples.

### What the corruption looks like

The probe is a Thai date-countdown answer, so the same words recur with unambiguous correct forms:

| correct | observed |
|---|---|
| `ปีใหม่` | `ปีใหม้` (mai tho for mai ek) |
| `สงกรานต์` | `สงกรานตค์์`, thanthakhat detached or missing |
| `ครับ` | `ครรับ` (doubled ro rua) |
| `คริสต์ศักราช` | `คริศต์ศักราช` (so sala for so suea) |
| `เช่น` | `เชน่` (tone mark displaced past the consonant) |
| `คำนวณ` | `คานวณ` (sara am lost) |
| `อีก` | `อีีก` (doubled sara ii) |

Thai is a sensitive detector rather than a special case: it runs ~3x more tokens per character than English, with many near-identical combining-mark tokens, so a perturbation surfaces as visibly broken text instead of a harmless paraphrase.

### Evidence

Prompt-length ladder built from a real captured agent request by dropping tool definitions and truncating the system prompt; the conversation itself is never touched, so every rung asks the identical question. N=10 per cell, corrupt / informative samples:

| prompt tok | 20394 | 16006 | 13369 | 9635 | 8556 | 6490 | 4675 | 2959 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| vLLM stock | 6/10 | 10/10 | 10/10 | 9/9 | 9/10 | 10/10 | 7/9 | 7/10 |
| vLLM, no MTP | 7/10 | 7/10 | 7/10 | 9/9 | 7/10 | 6/8 | 6/9 | 6/8 |
| **llama.cpp** | **0/10** | **0/10** | **0/10** | **0/10** | **0/10** | **0/10** | **0/10** | **0/10** |

issues.title: [Bug] modelopt NVFP4 MoE: mismatched w1/w3 global scales are detected, warned about, and then used anyway
issues.body_head:
### The behaviour

`ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE.process_weights_after_loading` fuses `gate_proj` and `up_proj` into `w13` and keeps only the **gate** per-tensor global scale:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py#L967-L975

```python
# Use a single gscale for w13.
if self.moe.is_act_and_mul and not torch.allclose(
    layer.w13_weight_scale_2[:, 0], layer.w13_weight_scale_2[:, 1]
):
    logger.warning_once(
        "w1_weight_scale_2 must match w3_weight_scale_2. Accuracy may be affected."
    )
w13_weight_scale_2 = layer.w13_weight_scale_2[:, 0].contiguous()
```

When the two differ, the up-projection half of `w13` is then dequantised with the gate half's global scale. The mismatch is detected, logged once, and the wrong scale is used anyway.

### How far apart they can be

Measured directly from the checkpoints on disk (reading only the `weight_scale_2` scalars — no GPU, no inference):

| checkpoint | modelopt | gate/up pairs | pairs that differ | ratio median / p99 / max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dealignai/GLM-5.3-Flash-ABLITERATED-NVFP4` | 0.45.0 | 12,384 | **8,563 (69.1%)** | 1.077 / 1.69 / **10.0** |
| `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` | 0.46.0 | 24,576 | 0 (0.0%) | — |
| `mazinb/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Uncensored-NVFP4` | 0.46.0-compatible-rtn | 24,576 | 0 (0.0%) | — |

All 43 MoE layers of the GLM checkpoint are affected; the worst layer has 272 of 288 experts mismatched. So this is not universal — the two modelopt 0.46 checkpoints tie the two scales exactly — but when a checkpoint does not tie them, the divergence is large and the whole model is affected.

Script used, if it is useful for triage:

```python
from safetensors import safe_open
# for each "...experts.N.gate_proj.weight_scale_2", compare with the
# matching "...up_proj.weight_scale_2" in the same checkpoint
```

### Why I am filing this rather than sending a patch

The detection is already there — the question is what to do on detection, and that is a design call I would rather not make unilaterally:

1. **Refuse to load** when the ratio exceeds some threshold, rather than warn and produce a quietly mis-scaled model. `warning_once` is easy to miss in a long startup log, and there is no runtime signal afterwards.
2. **Rescale** the `w3` half's per-block scales into the common global scale at load. The block scales are e4m3 with limited range, so this trades one error for another and needs care — I do not know whether it is a net win.

issues.title: [Bug] Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (qwen4_exp) + MTP: episodic 0% draft acceptance + repetition collapse in thinking block until max_tokens (SM120, bf16 KV, nightly @73029d4)
issues.body_head:
### Summary

`Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` (qwen4_exp / QSA+GDN hybrid, ModelOpt **NVFP4** checkpoint) served with **MTP speculative decoding** (`num_speculative_tokens: 3`) intermittently collapses into a **spec-decode state-divergence episode**: per-window MTP draft acceptance drops to exactly **0** (~2,000 drafted, 0 accepted), generation pins to the 1-token/step spec-decode floor (~66 tok/s vs 95–135 tok/s healthy at 50–85% acceptance on the same pod), and the model emits an **endless repetition loop inside the thinking block** (`finish_reason=length` after burning the entire token budget — one request ran 4h57m to the 1M-token window). Episodes last hours, then recover fully. Not context-length-bound, not GPU/host-health-bound, not pod-age-bound.

**Critical cross-model signal:** a second, architecturally unrelated model on the **same image** with the **same MTP config** — Gemma 4 26B (NVFP4, thinking on) — failed its garbage probe the same day with the identical signature ("finish_reason=length … repetition collapse"). Two different checkpoints, one engine build, same failure mode ⇒ engine-level MTP/spec-decode state bug, not a model-weight or quant issue.

### Environment

- vLLM: `0.28.1rc1.dev278`, nightly base commit `73029d42441321b631779db3475031f5ec26dd6c` (first nightly containing in-tree qwen4_exp support, PR #53896, merged 2026-08-31)
- GPU: 2× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), TP=2 (`g7e.12xlarge`)
- Model: `Inferact/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` (model_type `qwen4_exp`), thinking ON
- Spec: `--speculative-config {"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}` (in-checkpoint MTP head)
- KV cache: bf16/auto (QSA path is bf16-only), prefix caching on (~96% hit), `mamba-cache-mode align`, attention block 1600 tokens
- `--hf-overrides` YaRN rope scaling to 1M context
- Sampling defaults from checkpoint `generation_config`: temp 1.0, top_k 20, top_p 0.95, no repetition/presence penalty

### Fingerprint (full /metrics scrape, 10s windows, over the pod's life — 2,923 windows)

| signal | value |
|---|---|
| lifetime draft acceptance | 20% (5.35M drafted / 1.09M accepted) |
| healthy windows | acceptance 50–85%, solo stream 95–135 tok/s |
| collapse windows | acceptance **exactly 0.000/0.000/0.000** per position (~2,000 drafted), generation flat **64–70 tok/s** (the K=0 spec-decode floor: n=3 draft passes + 4-token verify per 1 accepted token) |
| hourly acceptance (NZ) | 02–07h 51–78% → 08h 31% → 09h 8% → 10h 12% → 11h 27% → 12h 4% → 13h 11% → **14h 66%** → 15h 18

issues.title: [Bug]: Sweep readiness uses the wrong address for equals options, repeated ports and IPv6
issues.body_head:
### Your current environment

Reproduced with the official `vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:v0.28.0-arm64` image on Linux/aarch64, plus pandas 3.0.5 for sweep summary export. The image's `vllm/benchmarks/sweep/server.py` is byte-identical to current main `58ad1f3` (SHA256 `441527a14f39b7f6b8c8c4c56d985dcfbec88492e141b8392a4990b01b224d21`). Model: SmolLM2-135M-Instruct, revision `12fd25f77366fa6b3b4b768ec3050bf629380bac`, running on CPU.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`ServerProcess._get_vllm_server_address()` manually scans separate `--host` / `--port` arguments, using the first occurrence. The native server accepts equals forms and uses the last repeated value. The sweep therefore waits on the wrong health endpoint even though the server has started correctly. IPv6 hosts also produce an invalid URL without brackets.

Minimal address reproduction:

```python
from vllm.benchmarks.sweep.server import ServerProcess

for args in [
    ["--host=127.0.0.2", "--port=8001"],
    ["--host", "127.0.0.2", "--port", "8000", "--port", "8001"],
    ["--host", "::1", "--port", "8001"],
]:
    server = ServerProcess(["vllm", "serve", "model", *args], [], show_stdout=False)
    print(server._get_vllm_server_address())
```

Actual: `http://localhost:8000`, `http://127.0.0.2:8000`, `http://::1:8001`.
Expected: `http://127.0.0.2:8001`, `http://127.0.0.2:8001`, `http://[::1]:8001`.

I also ran all three through native `vllm bench sweep serve`, with a real model server and benchmark process. They fail before benchmarking; the equivalent separate-option IPv4 control completes. A small patch using `argparse.parse_known_args()` and the existing `join_host_port()` makes all four runs complete, including the three cache resets and summary export.

### Before submitting a new issue...

Checked open PRs and issues for sweep server-address parsing, equals options, repeated ports and IPv6; found no matching fix. This is separate from #55491's readiness deadline change. Prepared with Codex.

issues.title: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731: deterministic wrong token on deep-context exact retrieval at 1-in-4 prompt lengths (reasoning off) — vLLM 0.28.0 + SGLang, reproduced on two hosted providers (DeepInfra, Baidu); one provider (OpenInference) is correct
issues.body_head:
## Summary
With reasoning disabled, an exact-string needle placed ~28k tokens into a ~57k-token prompt is returned with its last digit wrong (`PROVOCATIVE-8417` → `PROVOCATIVE-8411`) whenever the prompt length ≡ 3 (mod 4) tokens. It is deterministic (temperature 0, same wrong token every time), independent of the surrounding text (fully repetitive filler and a mixed filler both fail), and independent of the top-k backend. With reasoning enabled the same prompts are 16/16 correct. Needles early in the context, or with padding *after* the needle, are always correct.

The same checkpoint served by another provider (OpenRouter → OpenInference, fp8, reasoning_tokens=0) returns the correct code at the same prompt lengths; served by DeepInfra (fp8) and by Baidu (fp8) it returns the same wrong `8411` at every failing length. Four independent stacks agree on the wrong token; one provider does not — so this is not a property of the weights and not specific to our GPU.

issues.title: [Bug] PP>1 + spec decode: mamba align postprocess indexes block table by batch row of a stale (pp_size-old) batch -> recurrent state copied to wrong blocks (NaN / silent recall loss)
issues.body_head:
## Summary

With pipeline parallelism (PP > 1) **and** speculative decoding (MTP / EAGLE-style proposer) on a hybrid Mamba/GDN model (`qwen4_exp` in our fork, but the code path is the generic mamba-align postprocess), the mamba "align" postprocess indexes the block table by **batch row** while the request↔row mapping it is given (`idx_mapping`) belongs to the batch from `pp_size` steps ago. When batch composition changes between those steps (a request finishes or a new one is admitted), the recurrent (GDN/conv) state is copied between the **wrong physical mamba blocks** — possibly a live neighbour's, or a block already freed and reassigned. Downstream the GDN recurrence / MoE produce NaN logits or silently wrong tokens.

Observed on 8×RTX 3090, TP=2 PP=4, `num_speculative_tokens=3`, 1M context with prefix caching: NaN logits in mixed 4-way concurrent runs (nan_lines=5 per run) and a measurable recall drop on a 945K-token RULER-style probe (12/20 and 14/20 correct vs 16/20 with speculation off). `SPEC=0` is unaffected (the align copy only runs on the spec-decode acceptance path); a single request never reorders, so single-stream tests do not trigger it; the fused vs non-fused draft loop only changes timing.

## Where

V2 GPU model runner (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`): `execute_model()` starts with `update_pp_decode_requests()`, which pops the `PPHandler` FIFO entry from `pp_size` steps ago and passes its `idx_mapping` to `postprocess_sampled` → `MambaHybridModelState.postprocess_state` → `run_fused_postprocess_align`. The align kernel then used `batch_idx` to index the **gathered, batch-ordered** block table (whose contents are the T−1 batch's), i.e. rows from batch T−pp_size resolved against tables from batch T−1. Only ranks 0..pp−2 are affected (the last rank's mapping is current).

## Fix that worked for us

Index the align copies by **request slot** (`req_idx`, resolved through `idx_mapping`) into the request-ordered persistent block table (`BlockTables.block_tables[gid].gpu`) — the same `bt_row_idx = req_idx` convention `_copy_mamba_state_block` already uses — with the precopy synchronised accordingly. Zero extra cost. With the fix, the same mixed 4-way workload produced 0 NaN lines and the 945K recall returned to 15–16/20 (= speculation off). We also mask `-1` sentinel rows and rows past the live request count in the same path.

Reproducible on CPU with the real Triton kernel by constructing two consecutive batches with different request orde

issues.title: Possible response/request cross-talk: distinct non-overlapping requests return mismatched application binding values
issues.body_head:
## Summary

We observed an apparent request/response binding mismatch while serving a relevance workload through vLLM. This is a report of an observed symptom, not a confirmed vLLM defect; application-side parsing/model behavior remain possible explanations.

## Observation

Two separate requests, issued 13 seconds apart after a clean deployment, each returned an application-level opaque binding value that did not match the value associated with that request. The returned values differed from each other as well.

The two responses had distinct vLLM `cmpl-...` completion IDs, so they were not a duplicate/cached response. Both were recorded as the intended `relevance` model/adapter. The observation window had no overlapping full workload cycle; an intervening price-only cycle does not make relevance requests.

## Why this may matter

If a response can be associated with the wrong concurrent or recently completed request, downstream systems that bind generated structured output to source items can silently misattribute results. Our application fails closed on the mismatch, so no incorrect result was accepted.

## What we have and what is missing

- Available: timestamps, distinct completion IDs, requested-vs-returned application binding comparison, model/adapter identity, and workload-overlap evidence.
- Not available: a minimal standalone vLLM reproducer or enough sibling request tracing to distinguish server-side cross-talk from model-generated incorrect/echoed content.

Could maintainers advise whether this symptom matches any known issue or which request/response tracing fields and minimal reproducer configuration would best isolate it? We can provide sanitized logs and environment details if useful.

issues.title: [Tracking]: Watermarking hardening - compatibility tests and quality/performance regression monitoring
issues.body_head:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Follow-up to [the watermarking RFC #53916](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53916) and [the implementation PR #54053](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54053). This issue tracks automated compatibility tests and recurring quality/performance regression checks for watermarking in CI or nightly runs.

The RFC defines the design and reports initial evaluations. This issue tracks turning that validation into ongoing regression coverage as watermarking evolves. We should coordinate compatibility work with the implementation PR's existing tests and unsupported-feature assertions.

## Items:

* Feature compatibility: We want to exercise basic watermarking and detection functionality at a high API level, i.e. from a client perspective: Watermarked and non-watermarked generations are correctly identified as such. These tests should exercise a variety of feature combinations. E.g. speculative decoding, tool calling, structured output, parallelism (e.g. basic TP2 to begin with). The goal is to quickly surface failures when combining features, and provide an easy entrypoint for devs to fix them. Ideally these tests run as quickly as possible, so they might check only a small number of requests.

* Quality Regressions: Watermarking has some theoretical guarantees about distribution preservation, but we must check in practice to prevent regressions. These quality evals are heavier / slower, because they might run an entire dataset with potentially long generations to get statistically valid results. We could use GSM8K, or use a less saturated benchmark, as suggested by @simon-veitner-redhat. The simplest version could be to run the eval once on the watermarked model and compare performance to a reference value with some tolerance (which can be generated once offline). 
    * A more comprehensive approach is to run the entire eval multiple times (one time per key, perhaps 20 keys) to prove robustness over keys. There are statistical tests designed to surface model degradations, e.g.: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10144, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/34333
    * Note: The [watermarking RFC](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53916) showed a change in generation length, which is unexpected. We hope this disappears as we increase the number of keys n. However, @TQCB found some infinite generation cases in GSM8K, which might be related. issues.title: [Bug][ROCm] GLM-5.3-Flash indexer block-table mismatch on gfx942
issues.body_head:
## Environment

- 8x MI308X (gfx942), ROCm 7.2.3
- vLLM `0.28.1rc1.dev628+g2a02f6efe.rocm723`, `amd_aiter==0.1.21.post2`, `flydsl==0.3.2`
- GLM-5.3-Flash, TP8, bf16 KV, prefix caching enabled
- `index_kpool=4`, `index_topk=2048`, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`

## 1. Indexer block-table granularity mismatch

Long-prompt requests completed, but recall near the end degraded. The indexer cache uses 128-token storage pages (32 pooled entries), while the block table uses 640-token manager blocks:

- `allocate_kv_cache` honors `MLAAttentionSpec.storage_block_size`.
- `prepare_kernel_block_sizes` does not, leaving manager block IDs where physical page IDs are needed.

At `max_model_len=262144`, the 410-column table can address only `410 * 32 * 4 = 52480` token positions when interpreted by the pool-page consumer. This is a layout mismatch, not a model context-length limit.

Observed before the fix:

```text
cache_shape=(91780, 32, 132)  block_table_shape=(1, 410)
required_pooled_entries=40160
last_query_position=160639  max_selected_token_index=52479
```

Outside the table width, the gather masks the block-ID read and writes a zero scale. Inside the width, manager block IDs can name the wrong physical pages; this is not a fixed token offset.

PR #56381 makes the table use storage-page granularity. At the **same 262144-token setting**, it becomes `(1, 2050)`; manager block `b` expands to pages `5*b + [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]`.

## 2. Separate kpool-tail slot-mapping fault

A 7680-token prefill step also produced GPU memory-access faults. With `HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1`, the stack pointed to `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel`.

`KpoolTailSpec` reserves one circular block per request, but the generic mapper uses `position // 4` against a 32-column row. Its mapping should be left to `KpoolTailMetadataBuilder`. Fault occurrence depends on allocation; 7680 is an observed step size, not a universal threshold.

**PR #56381 addresses only problem 1.**

## Reproduction and validation scope

For problem 1, compare the same configuration before/after the PR with a roughly 160K-token prompt. Log the indexer cache shape, block-table shape/IDs, and the final prefill row's selected indices. Expected table entries are physical page IDs.

The model runs also used local fixes for FlyDSL `shrui(int)`, FP8 pack zero-extension, and problem 2. A stock build may fail on those paths first.

Separate 524288-window runs completed requests up to about 519K prompt tokens. These were dia

issues.title: [Doc]: prompt_lookup_min/prompt_lookup_max docstrings give the wrong defaults
issues.body_head:
### 📚 The doc issue

The `SpeculativeConfig` docstrings describe the defaults wrongly:

- `prompt_lookup_max` says it's "required when method is set to ngram".
- `prompt_lookup_min` says "Defaults to 1."

`__post_init__` does neither. If both are omitted, both are set to 5. If only one is given, the other copies it.

So `{"method": "ngram", "prompt_lookup_max": 4}` ends up with `prompt_lookup_min=4`, which means only exact 4-gram matches, not the 1 to 4 range the docstring suggests. The table in `docs/features/speculative_decoding/README.md` already describes the real behavior.

### Suggest a potential alternative/fix

Update the two docstrings to match `__post_init__` and the README, and add a unit test for these defaults, since none exists today. I'll open a PR.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

issues.title: [Bug]: Mixed prompt embedding masks are omitted from prefix cache keys, causing incorrect outputs
issues.body_head:
## Your current environment

- Tested source: `main` at `a2bc2ffb2c8bf46759c4bbeb88e2f4dc32968762`.
- Python 3.12.14; PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132; Transformers 5.16.1.
- NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090; driver 580.173.02; one GPU; FP16.
- vLLM editable source with the official **cu130 precompiled extension for the exact source commit**. This combination was exercised successfully in the GPU tests below.
- Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, revision `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`, using its real embedding weights.
- V2 Model Runner, FLASH_ATTN, eager execution, block size 16, greedy sampling, seed 0. `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn`, `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`, `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0`.

The original full before/after experiment used driver 580.173.02. The additional standalone-script runs on 2026-09-13 used driver 580.178.04 and produced the same token/cache results. The host runs Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS, glibc 2.35; the current `collect_env` reports CUDA toolkit 13.2.78. These are separately recorded runs rather than one unchanged host snapshot.

The affected unpatched function is also unchanged at `e52be1a62d3879b1202f4f355d3c3472b560c6f2`, checked on 2026-09-13. The numerical results below are from the explicitly identified tested revision, not a claim of rerunning the entire later `main`.

## Describe the bug

With `enable_prompt_embeds=True` and `enable_prefix_caching=True`, valid inputs with the same token IDs and supplied embedding tensor but different `prompt_is_token_ids` masks can reuse KV computed for a different effective input. The request succeeds, but its deterministic output depends on an earlier request's cache contents.

`prompt_is_token_ids[i]` selects either the model's learned embedding for the token ID (`True`) or the supplied embedding row (`False`). The prefix-cache key hashes the normalized token IDs and supplied tensor, but omits that selection mask. Embedding-backed positions are normalized to token ID 0, which is also a valid vocabulary ID.

In the reproducer, B alone generates `[9, 0] * 8`. After caching A, the **identical B** incorrectly hits 32 cached tokens and generates `[753] * 16`. Repeating A itself correctly hits 32 tokens.

### Scope

This is a functional correctness issue in the combination of mixed prompt embeddings and local prefix caching. The reproducer uses the public offline input interface, without external KV connectors, LoRA, concurrency, or stochastic sampling. It does not establish a failure in ordinary text-only reques

issues.title: DSpark checkpoints exported in fill-in (DFlash 1+N) layout silently serve with <1% acceptance: the optional layout flag is absent from their configs, and the default anchor-first sampler is wrong for them
issues.body_head:
Serving a DeepSpec-trained DSpark drafter on vLLM 0.27.1 produced a ~0.9% acceptance rate with no error or warning anywhere. The checkpoint was healthy; the failure was a layout mismatch that vLLM resolves silently in the wrong direction.

**What we observed.** The drafter was trained in the DFlash-style fill-in layout (`1 + N` query positions, anchor acts as the bonus token, every non-anchor position is a mask slot to fill). vLLM's `DSparkSpeculator` defaults to `sample_from_anchor=True` (the native DSpark layout: anchor is the first *predicted* token), and our draft configs carried no `sample_from_anchor` key the loader could use to detect the difference — so an anchor-position output was consumed as a predicted token and every subsequent position conditioned on the wrong context.

The absence of the key is worth explaining, because the field does exist upstream: `sample_from_anchor` was added to speculators' DFlash/DSpark configs only recently ([speculators #760](https://github.com/vllm-project/speculators/pull/760), 2026-07-13, defaulting to `True` for DSpark and `False` for DFlash, and serialized with the rest of the config; wired into vLLM's DSpark loader by [#48639](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48639), 2026-07-20). It remains an *optional* field, and export paths that predate it or bypass the speculators config dump still emit configs without it — both of our checkpoints, exported by a training pipeline built on a speculators fork (0.7.0.dev176), do. A consumer then has no choice but to fall back to the family default.

Because nothing raises, this presents only as "a terrible drafter": aggregate acceptance under 1%, per-position acceptance collapsing after position 0, and a trained-in-vain loss curve. We initially attributed exactly this symptom to an exposure-bias training bug and discarded two checkpoint families before measuring.

**One-line fix, measured.** Adding `"sample_from_anchor": false` to the draft config copy (no weight or system-package change; stock vLLM 0.27.1, all shims via PYTHONPATH) flips acceptance in place — same weights, same engine, same data, only the layout flag differs:

| checkpoint | default layout | `sample_from_anchor: false` | pairing granularity |
|---|---|---|---|
| an older 5-epoch teacher-forced draft — **main evidence** | **0.85%** | **47.4%** agg / 7.11 tokens per round | full 100-sample runs on **both** sides |
| draft B (full run) — corroborating | 0.089% | **43.3%** | smoke probes (~10K drafted

issues.title: [Bug][ROCm][Attention][KV Connector] DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.x DSA sparse-MLA decode is garbage under CUDA graphs in PD-disaggregation (remote-prefilled KV)
issues.body_head:
## Summary
In PD-disaggregated serving on ROCm/MI300X (MoRIIO KV connector, WideEP DP8/EP8), the **decode** engine emits degenerate repeated-token garbage (`locklocklock…` / `!!!`) for **remote-prefilled** requests whenever decode runs under **any CUDA-graph capture** (`FULL`, `PIECEWISE`, or `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`). With `DECODE_CUDAGRAPH_MODE=NONE` (eager) the identical stack decodes **coherently**. Colocated (non-disagg) serving and vLLM v0.27.1 are unaffected.

## Environment
- vLLM **0.28.0** (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.28.0`), AITER 0.1.19, ROCm 7.2.3
- 2× **MI300X (gfx942)**, RoCEv2; KV connector = **MoRIIOConnector** (WRITE mode), `block_size=1`, fp8 KV
- Models: **GLM-5.3-FP8** and **GLM-5.1-FP8** (both `GlmMoeDsa`, DeepSeek-V3.2-style **DSA sparse-MLA**)
- Topology: 1P1D **WideEP DP8/EP8**; MTP on or off (does not matter)

## How to reproduce
1. Launch 1P1D PD-disagg (MoRIIO WRITE) — e.g. the AMD harness `.buildkite/amd-disagg/run-slurm-disagg-test.sh` with `WIDE_EP_MODE=1 MORIIO_READ_MODE=0` — using `DECODE_CUDAGRAPH_MODE=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`.
2. Send any request → decode returns `locklocklock…` (garbage).
3. Set `DECODE_CUDAGRAPH_MODE=NONE` (eager) → decode is coherent. (`FULL` and `PIECEWISE` are each garbage too.)

## Expected behavior
Decode under CUDA graphs produces the same coherent output as eager decode (and as colocated single-node / vLLM v0.27.1).

## Isolation — what did NOT fix it vs what WORKED
We walked the full transfer→decode path with per-step, on-device instrumentation applied identically to both engines.

**Did NOT fix it (still garbage), i.e. ruled out as the cause:**
- **KV-cache content / transfer** — the transfer is complete and **bit-exact** (producer == consumer bytes for every layer, including the sparse-indexer k_cache). Explicitly transferring the indexer k_cache changed nothing.
- **MoRI library version** — swapping v1.1.0 ↔ commit `42e895472b08` (the version used by the working v0.27.1 recipe) made no difference.

- **KV dtype** — reproduces with **fp8 and bf16** (so not an fp8-scale/dequant issue).

issues.title: [Bug]: NaN vision embeddings with multi-budget encoder CUDA graphs sharing a pool
issues.body_head:
### Environment

Observed while validating #56922 on NVIDIA H20, TP=1, BF16, no LoRA, Python 3.12, Torch 2.13.0+cu132 and the CUDA FlashAttention vision backend. Model: Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct, revision 66285546d2b821cf421d4f5eb2576359d3770cd3. Python source before the mitigation: 873804d1e9 from that PR; precompiled native extensions were reused. A fresh full native build and a complete collect_env dump are not available for this observation.

### Observed behavior

With V2 E-only encoder CUDA graphs and the default nine token budgets [64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096,8192,16384], a 1280x720 image (1196 visual tokens, replaying budget 2048) produced NaN embeddings and incorrect generated answers. This was observed on two H20 nodes. A 224x224 image (64 tokens) remained correct.

The diagnostic sequence was small image -> large image -> small image. Each graph result was compared with ordinary eager and eager using the same padded graph input buffers. Encoder graphs were enabled with cudagraph_mm_encoder=True, decoder cudagraph_mode=NONE, mm_encoder_only=True, max_model_len=16384, max_num_seqs=32, and limit_mm_per_prompt={"image":2,"video":0}.

| Diagnostic condition | Observation |
|---|---|
| Ordinary eager | Correct |
| Eager using identical padded buffers | Correct |
| Only budget 2048 captured | Correct |
| Nine budgets sharing one graph pool | Large-image output contains NaNs |
| Nine budgets, a new graph pool handle for each capture | Correct |
| Shared pool, zero-initialized varlen attention output | Correct |

Separate pools were a diagnostic monkeypatch to _capture_budget_graph, not a supported configuration switch. These observations do not establish that pool sharing itself is invalid.

### Narrow deterministic regression

The test added in #56922 can expose unwritten padding without loading a model:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_mha_attn.py \
  -k graph_replay_keeps_padding_finite -v
```

The test captures BF16 attention with 256 rows, fills the captured output with NaN, changes cu_seqlens to make only 128 rows active, and replays. Without output initialization, the finite-padding assertion fails. With initialization, the output is finite and valid rows match an independent attention reference. This demonstrates unwritten output padding; it does not by itself prove how padding contaminates valid tokens in the full model.

### Expected behavior and open investigation

Valid encoder embeddings should remain fin

issues.title: [Bug][Reasoning] kimi_k3: non-streaming path classifies truncated reasoning as content (inconsistent with streaming path)
issues.body_head:
### Report

The `kimi_k3` reasoning parser's non-streaming fallback misclassifies truncated reasoning output as `content`, leaving `reasoning_content` as `null`. The streaming path classifies the exact same output as reasoning, so the two paths disagree.

### Root cause

`KimiK3ReasoningParser.extract_reasoning` in `vllm/reasoning/kimi_k3_reasoning_parser.py` (main @ f94666b60d):

```python
m_open = self._think_open_re.search(model_output)
content_start = m_open.end() if m_open is not None else 0
# if there is no think channel at all, everything is content
if m_open is None and self._think_close_re.search(model_output) is None:
    return None, self._content_after_reasoning(model_output, request)
```

The key fact is on the template side: when thinking is enabled, the Kimi K3 chat template ends the prompt with the think **open** marker (`<|open|>think<|sep|>`) as a generation prefix — the model never generates the open marker itself. So in generated text:

- the open marker is (almost) always absent;
- the close marker (`<|close|>think<|sep|>`) is absent whenever the output is truncated (e.g. `max_tokens` smaller than the reasoning length) or generation stops early.

That combination falls into the branch above and the whole reasoning text is returned as `content` with `reasoning=None`.

Meanwhile, the streaming path in the same file (`extract_reasoning_streaming`) treats any text with no close marker as reasoning:

```python
# no close marker anywhere -> still reasoning
return DeltaMessage(reasoning=reasoning_delta)
```

So for identical truncated output: `stream=true` returns it as `reasoning_content`, `stream=false` returns it as `content`. This also diverges from the upstream basic parsers (`vllm/reasoning/basic_parsers.py`), where a missing end token means the whole output stays reasoning (`return model_output, None`).

### Repro

Serve Kimi K3 with `--reasoning-parser kimi_k3`, then:

```bash
curl http://<server>/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "auto",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "reason step by step: 3 apples cost 12 yuan, how much for 7?"}],
  "max_tokens": 10,
  "stream": false
}' | jq '.choices[0].message'
```

Returns:

```json
{
  "content": "The user asks to reason step by step about a math problem. I only need ",
  "reasoning_content": null
}
```

With `"stream": true`, the same generation arrives as `reasoning_content` deltas instead.

### Suggested fix

When thinking is enabled and nei

### Summary

Since #52501 (merged 2026-09-13) GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 cannot be served with MTP on `main`.
The engine fails while loading the draft model:

```
RuntimeError: NVFP4 weight_scale for layer 'parallel_lm_head' was never loaded (still NaN).
The checkpoint likely stores this layer as BF16 (not FP4). Fix: pass quant_config=None when
constructing this layer, or add it to the quantization ignore list.

issues.title: [Bug]: DiffusionGemma: tensor shape mismatch in post_norm under concurrent decode (inputs_embeds vs silently-clamped sc_embeds)
issues.body_head:
### Summary

Both the NVFP4 and bf16 checkpoints of DiffusionGemma-26B-A4B crash the vLLM engine under concurrent request load, with the identical error:

```
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (257) must match the size of tensor b (256) at non-singleton dimension 0
```

raised from `self.post_norm(inputs_embeds + sc_signal)` in `DiffusionGemmaSelfConditioning.forward()`. This kills the engine core process (`EngineDeadError` propagates to the API layer). It is **not deterministic at any fixed concurrency level** — across 4 independent runs (2 per checkpoint) it triggered at 4, 6, 6, and 16 concurrent users respectively, and never at 2 concurrent users.

This looks related to #50699 (same file, same "concurrent decode" trigger condition) but is a distinct bug — it reproduces at `--max-num-seqs 4`, well below the concurrency level where that issue's OOM appears, and the failure mode is a shape mismatch, not OOM.

### Root cause (traced to source)

Pulled `vllm/model_executor/models/diffusion_gemma.py` from the `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.1` image. The crash site is `DiffusionGemmaModelState._apply_self_conditioning`:

```python
for slot, idx in zip(decode_slots_np.tolist(), decode_idx_np.tolist()):
    start = int(query_start_loc_np[idx])
    end = int(query_start_loc_np[idx + 1])
    canvas = slice(start, end)
    soft = sc_embeds[slot, : end - start]
    inputs_embeds[canvas] = self.model.self_conditioning(
        inputs_embeds[canvas], soft.to(inputs_embeds.dtype)
    )
```

- `inputs_embeds[canvas]` slices from `_inputs_embeds_buf`, a large batch-wide buffer — `inputs_embeds[start:end]` with `end - start = 257` legitimately returns 257 rows.
- `soft = sc_embeds[slot, :end - start]` slices from `self.diffusion_states.self_conditioning_embeds`, a **fixed-size per-slot buffer** shaped `[max_num_reqs, canvas_length, hidden_size]` where `canvas_length=256` for this checkpoint. PyTorch tensor slicing past the end of a dimension does not raise — it silently clamps. `sc_embeds[slot, :257]` on a 256-length dim quietly returns 256 rows.

Net effect: `inputs_embeds[canvas]` has 257 rows, `soft` is silently clamped to 256, both get passed into `self_conditioning.forward()` → `post_norm(inputs_embeds + sc_signal)` → shape mismatch, every time, with exactly these numbers.

**Open question**: why `end - start` (from `query_start_loc_np`, vLLM's scheduler output) is 257 instead of ≤ `canvas_length` for some request in some batches — that span computation lives in the sched

issues.title: [Bug]: Triton fused MoE incorrectly indexes per-channel weight scales with per-tensor activations
issues.body_head:
### Your current environment

Component validation environment:
- GPU: NVIDIA L20
- PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu129
- CUDA reported by PyTorch: 12.9
- Input dtype: BF16 for the scale-indexing reproducer

The component experiments used an overlay of relevant vLLM Python sources
with an existing compiled runtime, rather than a complete build at one
revision. The affected code was subsequently checked at
`00b7847c8036b667742b4efb21aab1de51fd4721`;

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`QuarkW8A8Int8MoEMethod` supports static per-tensor activation scales
together with per-output-channel weight scales. However, the legacy
Triton MoE path uses the activation quantization flag to select both
activation-scale and weight-scale indexing.

For this combination, `per_act_token_quant=False`, so the kernel takes
the tensor-scale branch even though the weights have per-channel scales.
It consequently reads the weight scales using the wrong layout.

This affects the existing static INT8 path independently of its planned
migration to the MoE oracle.

### Expected behavior

Activation and weight scales should be indexed independently:

- A1/A2: use the loaded static scalar activation scales.
- W13/W2: use the scale belonging to the routed expert and output channel.

Changing relevant weight scales should affect the corresponding
computation, while changing scales belonging only to unrouted experts
should not affect the output.

### Observed behavior and reproduction outline

A component probe used:
- 4 experts
- Hidden size and intermediate size of 128
- 8 tokens, top-k=2
- BF16 inputs
- Static activation scales and nonuniform per-channel weight scales
- No bias, with router weights applied on the output side

The probe exercised Quark weight creation and post-load processing,
then its existing `apply()` path.

With fixed weights, inputs, and routing, multiplying all W13 channel
scales of expert 3 by 4 produced no output change, although that expert
was selected by four routing slots.

An experimental patch separating weight-scale layout from activation
quantization made this perturbation affect the output. The corrected
legacy and manually constructed modular paths also produced identical
BF16 outputs for the covered case.

These are component-level observations, not a completed model evaluation
or full regression result. The modular comparison bypassed backend
selection and does not establish static INT8 oracle support.

There are two related problems:

1. `int8_w8a8_m

issues.title: [Bug][DSA] Complete sparse top-k output after DeepSelect detects a NaN
issues.body_head:
## Summary

[vLLM #58215](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58215) correctly bounds DeepSelect's NaN sentinel before sparse-index remapping, fixing the illegal-memory-access path. A follow-up correctness defect remains: when DeepSelect sees any NaN with `abort_when_nan_found=False`, it writes only `output_idx[row, 0] = 0x3f3f3f3f` and returns. It leaves the other `index_topk - 1` output slots untouched.

The V4.1 sparse MQA path reuses caller-owned `col_indices_buffer` across steps. `SparseMQAIndexer.forward` clears `topk_indices_buffer`, but not that DeepSelect scratch. Thus #58215 maps the first sentinel to `-1`, while the other unwritten slots retain prior-row indices. Since those stale columns are normally in `[0, width)`, they pass the new bound and are remapped as real attention positions.

This is not a second OOB access: it is silent stale top-k selection after a NaN row.

## Source evidence

- vLLM calls DeepSelect with `abort_when_nan_found=False` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/indexer_topk.py`.
- The pinned DeepSelect source (`d96d33afe1fa`; current DeepSelect main has the same behavior) implements `take_action_when_have_nan` by writing only slot 0 and returning.
- V4.1 allocates `col_indices_buffer` once in `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_indexer.py`; `vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_mqa_indexer.py` does not reset it per forward.

## Proposed vLLM-side repair

Before calling DeepSelect, replace NaN sparse logits in rows with `end > topk` by `-inf` in place. DeepSelect then produces a complete top-k from finite candidate columns. Keep #58215's `c < width` remap bound as the final safety guard.

A post-sentinel refill is not sufficient: the selector never ranked the other slots. For an all-NaN row, this policy deterministically chooses valid `-inf`-tied candidate columns rather than using stale data.

## Regression

Extend `test_sparse_topk_remap_bounds_nan_rows` to prefill `col_indices` with a valid-looking poison value, insert NaNs in a row, and assert the remapped set equals:

```python
logits.nan_to_num(nan=-float("inf")).topk(topk, dim=-1).indices
```

The #58215-only implementation fails this test because the poison survives beyond slot 0.

## Observed serving impact

On a GB200 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash disaggregated lane, #58215 removed the IMA but changed speculative acceptance length by -3.39% in a controlled mount-only A/B, while raw sparse scoring remains faster per token. This issue identifies the missing contract handling
